## 2. How to run it

Everything is already installed and configured. Node is managed by nvm.

```bash
# interactive terminals pick this up from ~/.zshrc automatically.
# a non-interactive shell (like an agent's Bash tool) does NOT, so prefix with:
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . /opt/homebrew/opt/nvm/nvm.sh; nvm use 22
export COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0
```

Toolchain: Node 22.23.2 (nvm), Yarn 3.2.1 (via corepack), Docker 28.4.0, gh 2.100.0 (authed as angrapsas).
Do NOT use Node 24 — some suites fail on it. Homebrew also has a Node 26 that nvm shadows.

### Two separate apps

**A. The monorepo** at `~/medusa` — the actual Medusa source, what we make PRs against.

```bash
cd ~/medusa
yarn install                                    # ~1 min
yarn build                                      # ~2.5 min, 80 packages
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard dev          # admin dashboard dev server on :5173
yarn workspace @medusajs/ui storybook           # design system on :6006
```

**B. A scaffolded store** at `~/my-store` — created with create-medusa-app, used to click around a
real running store. Uses PUBLISHED medusa packages from npm, NOT the local source, so changes to
`~/medusa` do NOT show up here.

```bash
docker start medusa-postgres                    # postgres:15 on :5433, db `my_store`, postgres/postgres
cd ~/my-store/apps/backend && npm run dev       # admin at :9000/app
```

Admin login exists (created during Sprint 0). Store is seeded: 4 products, 20 variants, 2 orders,
1 region (Europe/EUR), 1 sales channel.

**Which one to use:** :5173 to see your own dashboard changes. :9000 to see a fully working store
with data. They are different codebases.

## 3. Known broken things (all upstream Medusa, not our fork)

Our fork only adds STUDENTS.md and course files on top of Medusa 2.17.2. These are real upstream bugs.

**1. 467 unit tests fail on a clean checkout.** `@medusajs/icons` 464/464 and `@medusajs/ui` 3/40.
All from one cause: `packages/design-system/icons/package.json` declares
`react: "^18.3.1 || ^19.0.0"` in devDependencies, so Yarn nests react@19.2.6 inside that package
while `react-dom@18.3.1` stays hoisted at root. React 19 elements + React 18 renderer =
"Objects are not valid as a React child". Fix: scoped resolution `"@medusajs/icons/react": "^18.3.1"`
in root package.json — precedent already exists there for `@redocly/cli/react`.
**68 of 70 packages pass.** Confirmed by three of us independently. NOT your machine.

**2. The standalone dashboard dev server renders a blank page.**
`packages/admin/dashboard/vite.config.mts` defines only 3 of the 6 globals the source needs.
Missing: `__AUTH_TYPE__`, `__JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY__`, `__MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE__`.
`src/lib/client/client.ts:3` throws a ReferenceError before React mounts. The bundled admin at
:9000 works because `admin-bundler/src/utils/config.ts:52-57` defines all six. Config was last
touched 2024-10-09; the source added those globals in late 2025. Nobody has fixed it.
Workaround already in the repo: `vi.hoisted()` in three spec files sets the globals for tests.

**3. Form validation errors never display anywhere in the dashboard.**
`@hookform/resolvers@3.4.2` with `zod@4.2.0`. Resolvers v3 doesn't understand zod 4 errors, so
instead of putting them in form state it throws. **116 files use zodResolver, 104 render
`<Form.ErrorMessage />`, and none of them can show anything.** Submitting an invalid form just
silently refuses. Verified by running validation directly: errors exist with messages, they just
never reach the form.

**#58 in one paragraph (I get asked about this):** completing a cart when an item sold out returned
a 400 with no cart, so the storefront could not show which item was the problem. The error comes
from `ensureInventoryLevels` in the inventory module, thrown as `NOT_ALLOWED`. The promotion-limit
and subscription errors from the same workflow are also `NOT_ALLOWED`, so the route could not branch
on type. I attached the existing `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY` code to the error at its source and added
a `statusOKErrorCodes` list to `packages/medusa/src/api/store/carts/[id]/complete/route.ts`.
Rejected alternatives: allow the whole `NOT_ALLOWED` type (swallows the other two), pre-check stock
(extra query on every checkout and still racy), new error type (the HTTP error handler does not know
it, so other routes 500). Cost: handled errors now live in two lists, and the code appears in other
routes' error bodies, which required updating two reservation tests.

The team's second tech showcase was **Ponytail** (https://ponytail.dev,
github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail, MIT), a Claude Code plugin that injects a decision ladder
(stdlib → native platform feature → reuse existing project code → only then write new code) so the
agent stops over-engineering. Published benchmarks: 54% less code, 27% faster, 20% lower API cost,
with validation and security never simplified away. Commands: `/ponytail-review` (scan the current

## 9. Lessons learned

Medusa core is deliberately minimal; the plugin ecosystem fills feature gaps. **Before proposing
anything, search externally, not just the repo.** Ideas that looked like gaps but already exist as
official or community plugins: Shopify migration (Medusa's own MCP server does it), sales analytics
dashboard (Agilo and rsc-labs plugins), abandoned cart recovery (community plugin + Medusa guide).

The proposals that survive are ones a plugin **cannot** add — engine behavior, admin API routes,
core defaults. That's why #16 and #23 hold up.

Also verified as genuinely missing: order CSV import (products have import+export, orders have
export only), customer export, and **a count of how many times a product has sold** —
`order_line_item` has indexed `product_id` and `variant_id` plus `quantity`, so the data is there
and indexed; nobody surfaced it. That last one is a natural sequel to #9 (order count + lifetime
spend for customers, which lefecko already merged).

From Sprint 1:
- **Read the code before trusting an issue's scope.** #32 already existed, #16 was smaller than written.
- **Claim issues and get spec review comments at the start of the sprint.** Sprint 1 all landed on the last day.
- **Never paste issue/PR text copied from the terminal.** It mangled #32 and #40 twice. Save to a file and
  post with `gh issue edit N --body-file <file>` / `gh pr create --body-file <file>`.
- **Run parallel work in separate git worktrees**: `git worktree add ~/medusa-<n> -b <branch> origin/develop`.
- **Watch AI scope creep.** On #11 it added a whole-number rule for weights nobody asked for. Tell it to stick to
  the acceptance criteria and check commit messages before every commit.

From Sprint 2:
- **Sprint 0 lost D4/D5 points because no issue comment linked the logs.** The link has to open the
  log file itself, not the folder. One "AI Assistance" comment per contributor per issue.
- **The error you are looking for is often not where the obvious code is.** On #58 I assumed
  `confirm-inventory.ts` because it already used `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY`. That step does not run on
  cart completion at all. Trace the real path before designing.
- **Tag an error at its source, match on the tag at the boundary.** Beats pattern-matching messages
  or widening a type list that other errors share.
- **Every PR needs the Tech Debt section**, split into Introduced (a tradeoff you chose) and
  Encountered (pre-existing, scoped out). Sprint 3 adds Test Evidence on top of it.
- **Reviews must be substantive.** On #89 I checked out the branch, ran it, and reverted the author's
  fix to confirm his new test actually failed. That is the kind of thing worth writing down in the
  review.
- **Diagrams need a legend and annotations or they lose points**, even when the structure is right.

## 11. Conventions to follow

- Prettier: no semicolons, double quotes, 2-space indent, ES5 trailing commas. `npx prettier --check <files>`
- Files kebab-case, types PascalCase, functions camelCase, constants SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, DB fields snake_case
- Commit style is mixed on the team: conventional (`feat(dashboard): ...`) and plain imperative both appear
- **Changesets required** — add one as a separate `chore:` commit. See `.changeset/` for format
- PR description format: What / Why / How / Testing, in plain prose, first person. Include the
  command to run the tests. No checklists, no bolded headers — teammates don't use them
- `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailers appear on some commits (lefecko uses them, upstream Medusa
  does too). Not required
- AI logs go to `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<username>/YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`. Link the log from
  the issue or PR it documents, as a full URL that opens the file itself, not the folder
- My commits: short plain subject only ("Add ...", "Fix ..."), no body, no Co-Authored-By line
- Every PR gets a teammate review with the course rubric. **Never self-approve or self-merge**

**New in Sprint 3 (see `sprint3.md` for the full text):**
- Every PR description needs a **Test Evidence** table (one row per AC: test, level, source of the
  expected value) on top of the Tech Debt section. The source of an expected value may never be
  "what the code currently returns"
- A PR merges only after a teammate approves **the latest commit**. Pushing after an approval
  invalidates it
- A **spec review comment on the issue, before coding**, that states what the reviewer checked
- Use `Closes #<issue>` in the PR description and attach issues and PRs to the sprint milestone
- D6 mutation testing uses **StrykerJS** (Jest runner for backend packages, Vitest runner for the
  dashboard), run only on the files the PR changed, with before/after JSON reports committed

## 12. How I like to work

- Find the code myself first, then use AI to check my understanding. The course grades this
  ("concept location") and I have to be able to explain every line of my own PRs
- Verify claims by running things, don't assert from reading. Prove a test fails without the fix
- Don't post to GitHub (issues, PRs, comments, reviews, tags) without showing me the exact text first
- Keep writing plain. No em dashes, no AI-sounding scaffolding. Match my teammates' register

you don't write it twice.

```markdown
## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]

**AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you
checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
```

**How to fill it in:**
- One row per acceptance criterion from D2. For bug reports, use the Expected Behavior instead. For
  PRs that change no product behavior (for example CI changes), write "N/A" and explain why.
- **Test(s):** the test name (and file, if not obvious). If checked manually, write `Manual:`
  followed by the steps and what you saw. If an AC is tested both ways, list both in the same row.
- **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E`, or `manual`.
- **Source of expected value:** where the expected result comes from. One of: `AC`,
  `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or `other` (explain). **The current output of
  your own code is not a valid source**; a test whose expected value was copied from what the code
  returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
- **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
- You may use AI to draft this section, but you are responsible for checking that it is accurate.

**Example:**

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: An end date before the start date is rejected with an error | `outOfOffice.schema.test.ts > rejects end before start` | unit | AC |
| AC2: The away badge appears on the booking page during the out-of-office window | `booking-ooo.e2e.ts > shows away badge in window` | E2E | AC |
| AC3: The badge text is readable in dark mode | Manual: enabled dark mode, opened the booking page during the window, badge text is readable | manual | issue discussion |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** AC3 depends on visual contrast, which our test setup does not check.

**If your fork has no CI that runs your tests** (ours does not run on PRs), include the command(s)
you ran and a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).

**Reviewers add one line to the code review rubric** (from Sprint 1 D4):

| Criterion | Score (1-10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Test evidence - does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | | |

### D6 - Mutation Testing (15 pts, individual) - NEW

**What it is.** A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (**mutants**), such as
flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test
fails, the mutant is **killed**. If all tests pass, the mutant **survived**: your tests did not
notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.

**What to do.** For one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests
(**CSCI 535: two such issues**; your small issue may be one of them):

1. Run a mutation testing tool **on the source files changed by your PR(s) for that issue**. Do not
   run it on the whole project.
2. Using the tool's report, **analyze every surviving mutant**: is it **equivalent** (it behaves
   exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a **gap** in your
   tests? If there are more than 10 survivors, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines
   your PR added or changed.
3. **Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a surviving mutant** that revealed a gap.
   Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent),
   say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
4. Answer the questions in the template.

**Evidence.** Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (**StrykerJS: add `"json"` to
`reporters`**). Commit the report from the first run and the re-run as
`docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json`. The mutation
scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in
the "after" report.

**A tool is required. Manual mutation does not count.**

| Stack | Tool |
|---|---|
| **TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa)** | **StrykerJS with the Jest runner** |
| TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
| Go | Gremlins or go-mutesting |

**Note for us:** Medusa is mixed. Backend packages use **Jest**, the dashboard uses **Vitest**.
Pick the runner that matches the files the PR changed.

**Set it up early.** Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services,
choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits
the configuration used. **You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to)**, as long as you
run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.

**Common problems to watch for:**
- **The tool stops before mutating.** Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any
  selected test fails, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where the baseline
  run helps). *Relevant to us: see HANDOFF section 3 and issue #98.*
- **Tests run against built code.** If tests run against compiled output (a `dist` folder) instead
  of the source, mutants in the source are never seen. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing,
  or choose tests that run on source. *Relevant to us: the integration tests load `dist`.*
- **Tests need services.** Some suites need a database or another service running. Start them first.
- **False survivors.** If you limit which tests run, make sure the tests that cover the mutated
  files are included. Otherwise mutants some test would catch are reported as survived or not
  covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
- **Long runs.** Mutating only the files changed by the PR keeps run time manageable.

**If you are blocked:** ask teammates first, someone may have a working setup. Still stuck, tell the
TA **as early as possible**, with the errors and the AI log of what you tried. The TA may approve
running the tool on a different issue or part of the code. **Problems reported at the end of the
sprint will not excuse a missing D6.**

**Submission:** `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-angrapsas.md`, using this template:

```markdown
# Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <issue title>

**PR(s):** #...
**Tool:** ...
**Config:** [link; credit the teammate if you reused their setup]
**Command:** `...`
**Reports:** [before](reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json) · [after](reports/<issue#>-<username>-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before ...% → after ...%

## Surviving mutants

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| | | | |

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [link] · Test: [file > test name] · Kills: [mutant location]

## Questions

1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?
2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the
   requirements? Explain.
3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and
   what did you verify or correct? If AI was not used, write "N/A."
```

**Rubric:**

| Criterion | Points |
|---|---|
| Tool run on the files changed by the PR; configuration, command, results and reports committed | 4 |
| Surviving mutants analyzed correctly (equivalent vs test gap, with explanation) | 4 |
| At least one new or strengthened test kills a surviving mutant; re-run confirms it | 4 |
| Answers to the questions show understanding, not just description | 3 |

**CSCI 535: the D6 score is the average of the two submissions.**

## Summary
This adds admin screens to create and edit bundles, and shows a bundle's components on its product page and on order pages. It also shows which bundles are blocking the deletion of a product or variant, and lets the admin return a single item from a bundle. Store owners can manage kits and partial returns without API calls, and staff packing orders can see which items to ship.

## User Story
As a store owner, I want to create, view and process returns for bundles in the admin dashboard so that I can manage kits without writing API calls.

## User Scenario
The store owner opens Products, clicks "Create bundle", enters a title, uploads images, picks the "Cameras" category, searches for and adds the camera body, lens and bag, sets each quantity and price, and saves. The bundle's product page lists its components. On an order that contains the bundle, the order page shows the components that need to be shipped. Later, a customer sends back only the bag. The owner opens the return form, picks the bag under "Camera kit", sees the $83.33 refund, and lowers it because the bag came back damaged. When the owner later tries to delete the lens, the dashboard shows that "Camera kit" uses it, with a link to the bundle.

## Scope
Medium: new create/edit forms, a components section on the product page, a components list on the order page, a clearer blocked-deletion error and a component picker in the existing return form, reusing the existing product form fields, variant picker and inventory-kit display.

## Source
Parent issue #101 (product bundles), from the project issue tracker.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. An admin can create a bundle by entering the normal product fields (title, description, images, categories), picking variants, setting quantities and setting prices.
2. An admin can edit a bundle's product fields, components, quantities and prices.
3. Invalid input shows inline errors and blocks saving: fewer than 2 components, a quantity of 0 or less, a missing price.
4. Errors from the server (for example, a component is itself a bundle) are shown to the admin, and anything they entered is kept.
5. A bundle's product page lists its components and their quantities.
6. An order page shows the components of every bundle in the order, including which components have been returned.
7. When deleting a product or variant is blocked because bundles use it, the dashboard lists those bundles, each with a link, instead of a generic error.
8. The admin return form lets the admin pick individual components of a bundle line item, and shows each component's refund amount.
9. The return form stops the admin from returning more of a component than is left to return, and shows server errors.
10. The admin can change the refund amount on a bundle-component return the same way as on any other return.

## Out of Scope
- Storefront UI
- A dedicated bundles page or upsells on component products

## Open Questions
- Should "Create bundle" be its own button on the Products page, or an option inside the existing create product form?
- Should the product list have a filter or badge that marks which products are bundles?
- This issue depends on the backend bundle API issue, and its return form part (criteria 8-10) depends on the checkout and returns issue.

## Summary
This makes bundles work from checkout through returns. Checkout names the exact item that is out of stock instead of giving a generic error. When an order is placed, the system saves each item's share of the bundle price. A shopper or admin can then return just one item from a bundle and get that share back. Shoppers understand failed orders and can keep the parts of a kit they want, and store owners get refunds they can predict.

## User Story
As a shopper, I want to know which item in a bundle is out of stock, and to return a single item from a bundle I bought, so that I can complete my purchase and get a fair refund for what I don't keep.

## User Scenario
A shopper has a "Camera kit" in their cart. The lens sells out before they check out, so placing the order fails with a message saying the lens is out of stock. The lens comes back into stock and they buy the kit for $1,000. The camera, lens and bag normally cost $800, $300 and $100, so the order saves shares of $666.67, $250.00 and $83.33. A week later they return only the bag: they get $83.33 back, one bag goes back into stock, and they keep the camera and lens.

## Scope
Medium: it changes the error message in the existing cart inventory check (`packages/core/core-flows/src/cart/steps/confirm-inventory.ts`), adds a share calculation when an order is placed, and extends the existing store and admin return workflows to accept a single bundle item, with no new data model.

## Source
Parent issue #101 (product bundles), from the project issue tracker; return and refund rules set by the owner.

## Acceptance Criteria
Checkout
1. If a bundle component is out of stock, the order is not placed and the error names that component.
2. If several components are out of stock, the error names all of them.
3. Items that aren't bundles still produce an error that names the variant.
4. If two shoppers try to buy the last available bundle at the same time, one order succeeds and the other gets the named-component error. Stock never goes negative.
5. Promotions and tax treat a bundle as one line item. Promotions aimed at a single component don't apply to the bundle.
6. Fulfilling a bundle line item ships all of its components together.

Refund shares
7. When an order with a bundle is placed, each component's share is saved on the order: (component normal price x component quantity) / (sum over all components) x bundle price paid.
8. Normal prices are taken in the order's currency and region at the time the order is placed.
9. After rounding to the currency's smallest unit, the shares add up exactly to the bundle price paid. Any leftover cents go to specific components chosen by a fixed rule, so the same order always gives the same shares.
10. If the bundle line item has a discount, the shares are worked out from the amount actually paid, not the list price.
11. Changing a component's or the bundle's price after the order is placed does not change the saved shares.
12. If a component has no normal price in the order's currency, the share is split by quantity, and placing the order still succeeds.

Returns
13. A return request (store or admin) can name one or more components of a bundle line item, with a quantity for each.
14. The refund for a returned component is its saved share multiplied by the quantity returned.
15. Only the returned component's stock is put back. Other components' stock is unchanged.
16. Returning every component of a bundle, in one return or several, refunds exactly the bundle price paid, without any cents lost or gained to rounding.
17. Returning the whole bundle as one item still works as it does today.
18. An admin can still override the refund amount on a specific return using the existing custom refund amount.
19. A request is rejected with a clear error when:
    - it returns more of a component than was bought or than is left after earlier returns
    - it names a component that isn't in that bundle
    - it returns a component from an order placed before the refund shares were saved
20. A shopper can only create returns for their own orders. Admin return actions require admin access.
21. Orders without bundles, and orders placed before this change, keep working unchanged.

## Out of Scope
- How the storefront displays the out-of-stock error or the return form
- Exchanges or claims for single bundle components
- Changing how refunds are paid out
- Admin return form (see the admin bundle screens issue)

## Open Questions
- Should the out-of-stock error also name the bundle (e.g. "Camera kit: Lens is out of stock"), or only the component?
- Should tax be included in the amount that gets split into shares, or should shares be worked out before tax and tax refunded separately?
- For orders placed before the refund shares were saved, should a single-component return be rejected (as written above), or should the shares be worked out at return time from current prices?
- Is splitting by quantity the right fallback when a component has no price in the order's currency, or should the bundle be blocked from sale in that currency instead?
- The checkout error part can start right away. The refund shares and returns depend on the backend bundle API issue, which defines a bundle's components and their variants.
```

## Summary

**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?

Part 2 of product bundles (#101): bundles now work from checkout through returns.

- Out-of-stock errors name the product, for example "Camera kit: Lens is out of stock." (at add-to-cart and at checkout).
- When an order is placed, each bundle item's share of the price paid is saved on the order line.
- A shopper (store API) or admin can return a single item from a bundle. The refund is that item's share, and only that item goes back into stock.
- Checkout no longer oversells when two cart lines use the same stock (a bundle plus one of its items).

**Why** — Why are these changes relevant or necessary?

Closes #113. Shoppers need to know which item stopped their order, and store owners asked to accept returns of single bundle items with a fair, predictable refund.

**How** — How have these changes been implemented?

- Checkout: `confirmInventoryStep` (add-to-cart) and `reserveInventoryStep` (checkout) build their error with `insufficient-inventory-error.ts`, which resolves a short inventory item to the bundle item that uses it. The inventory module now checks stock per item and location across all lines of a reservation batch.
- Shares: a new `prepareBundleRefundSharesStep` in `completeCartWorkflow` splits the bundle line's total (after discounts, including tax) by each item's normal price and saves the result in the order line's `metadata.bundle`. The maths is in `bundle-refunds.ts`.
- Returns: return items accept `component_variant_id`. New steps `prepareBundleReturnItemsStep` and `prepareBundleReceiveItemsStep` validate the request and record the item and its refund in the return item's metadata. They're wired into the store return, admin request, receive, dismiss and confirm-receive workflows. The order module's return actions leave the bundle line's own quantities alone for these items, and on receipt add a credit line for the refund. Confirming receipt restocks only the item's inventory.
- Store API: `POST /store/returns` accepts an optional customer login. Returning a single bundle item requires the logged-in customer who owns the order.
- A changeset is included (patch).

**Testing** — How have these changes been tested, or how can the reviewer test the feature?

See Test Evidence below. To try it: create a bundle (`POST /admin/bundles`), buy it, fulfill it, then `POST /store/returns` with `component_variant_id` as the order's customer.

---

## Examples

```ts
// Checkout when the lens sold out
POST /store/carts/:id/complete
// 200 { type: "cart", error: { message: "Camera kit: Lens is out of stock.", type: "not_allowed" } }

// Saved on the order line (kit sold for $1,000; camera/lens/bag normally $800/$300/$100)
order.items[0].metadata.bundle.components
// [{ variant_id: "variant_camera", refund_share: 666.67, units: 1, ... },
//  { variant_id: "variant_lens",   refund_share: 250,    ... },
//  { variant_id: "variant_bag",    refund_share: 83.33,  ... }]

// Return only the bag (logged-in customer who owns the order)
POST /store/returns
{
  "order_id": "order_123",
  "items": [{ "id": "ordli_kit", "quantity": 1, "component_variant_id": "variant_bag" }],
  "return_shipping": { "option_id": "so_return" },
  "receive_now": true
}
// return.items[0].metadata.bundle_component = { variant_id: "variant_bag", title: "Bag", amount: 83.33 }
// The order's pending difference drops by 83.33; one bag goes back into stock.
```

---

## Design

**Decision:** A single-item return is a normal return line on the bundle's order line, with the returned item and its refund in the line's metadata. The refund is booked as an order credit line when the item is received.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Count the bag as 1/12 of a bundle (fractional quantity on the bundle line). Rejected: admins would see fractional quantities, the maths needs extra rounding, and restocking would still need custom code.
- Replace the bundle line with one line per item before the return ("unbundle"), then use the normal return flow. Rejected: it rewrites order and fulfillment history, which is risky for past orders.
- Use the return action's amount for the refund. Tried first: Medusa recalculates the saved order total from each line's returned quantities, not from action amounts, so the refund never showed. The credit line is the mechanism Medusa already uses to lower an order's total.

**Rationale:** It uses Medusa's existing extension points (metadata on return items and actions, credit lines), keeps order history intact, and needs no data migration.

**Consequences:**
- A returned item shows up as a credit line (`reference: "bundle_component_return"`) rather than as a returned quantity on the bundle line.
- The bundle line isn't marked as returned even when all its items are; the return items show what came back.
- Exchanges and claims don't support single bundle items.

**Other decisions:**
- **What is split:** the bundle line's total after discounts and including tax, so returning every item refunds exactly what was paid (AC 7, 10). Rejected: the subtotal before tax with tax refunded separately (more code, and the sum wouldn't equal what was paid).
- **Rounding:** each share is rounded down to the currency's smallest unit, and leftover cents go one each to the largest remainders, with the earlier item winning a tie. Partial returns spread a share by rounding the running total down, so they always add up to it (AC 9, 16). Rejected: rounding each share to nearest (doesn't always add up), and giving all leftover cents to the first item (less fair).
- **Missing price:** if an item has no price in the order's currency, the whole line is split by quantity (AC 12). Rejected: blocking the sale, and splitting only the unpriced item by quantity.
- **Older orders:** a single-item return from an order placed before shares were saved is rejected; returning the whole bundle still works (AC 19). Rejected: working shares out from today's prices (the refund would depend on later price changes).
- **Store login (owner-approved):** only single bundle item returns require the logged-in customer who owns the order. Guest returns of normal items and whole bundles work as before. Rejected: requiring login for all store returns (breaks guest returns), and leaving it open.
- **Whole bundle after a single item:** a whole-bundle return is only allowed for bundles none of whose items were returned. Rejected: allowing it (refunds the returned item twice).
- **Out-of-stock wording:** the error names the bundle and the item ("Camera kit: Lens is out of stock."); other products are named on their own ("T-shirt (L) is out of stock."). The error type and code are unchanged, so clients that check `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY` still work. Rejected: naming only the item (the shopper sees the kit in their cart), and keeping the generic message for non-bundles (AC 3).
- **Oversell fix in the inventory module (owner-approved):** stock is checked per item and location across all lines of a batch. Rejected: a pre-check in core-flows (an extra query on every checkout), and leaving it as tech debt.

---

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- Single-item returns are validated in a workflow step without a lock, so two simultaneous requests for the same item could both pass. Normal returns are checked inside the order module's transaction.
- The quantity of a requested or received single item can't be edited in place. The admin removes it and adds it again (the update workflows return a clear error).
- An admin can still send arbitrary metadata on exchange and claim items, which these changes don't validate. Return items are cleaned.

**Encountered:**
- `POST /store/returns` had no login check: anyone with an order ID can create a return. This is only closed for single bundle items (see Design).
- The inventory module checked each reservation line on its own, so two lines using the same stock could oversell. Fixed here; 4 existing inventory-module test fixtures reserved 6 units against a stock of 2 and were updated.
- `createAndCompleteReturnOrderWorkflow` with `receive_now` received every item of the order instead of the returned ones. It now receives the returned items.

---

## Test Evidence

|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: Out-of-stock bundle item is named; order not placed | `bundle-checkout-returns.spec.ts` "names the bundle component that is out of stock at checkout (AC 1)", "names the component when adding the bundle to the cart"; `insufficient-inventory-error.spec.ts` resolveInventoryShortages / formatInsufficientInventoryMessage | integration, unit | AC1; wording from the issue's open question ("Camera kit: Lens is out of stock") |
| AC2: Every out-of-stock item is named | "names every out-of-stock component (AC 2)"; unit "names every out-of-stock component (AC 2)", "lists several components of one bundle together" | integration, unit | AC2 |
| AC3: Items that aren't bundles name the variant | "names the variant of an item that isn't a bundle (AC 3)"; unit getVariantDisplayName tests | integration, unit | AC3 |
| AC4: Two shoppers, last bundle: one order, named error for the other, stock never negative | "lets one order through and names the component for the other; stock never goes negative"; "checks a bundle and a separate line for one of its components together"; inventory module "should check the stock for all reservations of one batch together" | integration | AC4 |

## Summary
This adds backend support for bundles: products made from several component variants, sold at their own price. A bundle behaves like any other product in the store API, with its own title, images, price and categories, and buying one reduces stock for each component. Store owners can then sell kits and deals, and shoppers can buy related items together in one purchase.

## User Story
As a store owner, I want to create a bundle from several product variants with its own price so that I can sell kits and deals.

## User Scenario
The store owner sends a request to create a "Camera kit" bundle with a title, images and the "Cameras" category, containing 1x camera body, 1x lens and 1x bag, priced at $899 in USD and €849 in EUR. The kit shows up on its own product page and in the Cameras category like any other product. Shoppers can add it to their cart, and buying it reduces stock for all three components. Later, the owner tries to delete the lens product and gets an error saying it is used in "Camera kit".

## Scope
Medium: one new workflow and admin create/update routes built on the existing inventory-kit links, plus a check added to the existing product and variant delete workflows, with no new data model and no migration.

## Source
Parent issue #101 (product bundles), from the project issue tracker.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. An admin can create a bundle by giving the normal product fields (title, description, images, categories), at least 2 component variants with a quantity for each, and prices per currency.
2. An admin can update a bundle's product fields, components, quantities and prices.
3. A bundle is returned by the store API like any other product: on its own and in category listings, with its title, images, price and categories.
4. The store API marks a product as a bundle and lists its components (variant and quantity), so other code can look up a bundle's components.
5. Placing an order for a bundle reduces stock for each component by its quantity multiplied by the number of bundles ordered.
6. A bundle shows as out of stock if any component is out of stock. Its available quantity is the lowest number of complete bundles the component stock can make.
7. A request is rejected with a clear error when:
   - it has fewer than 2 components
   - a component variant doesn't exist
   - a component doesn't track inventory
   - a component is itself a bundle
   - the same component is listed twice
   - a quantity is 0 or less
   - a price is missing or negative
8. A rejected create leaves no partial bundle behind (the workflow rolls back).
9. Users who aren't logged in as an admin can't create or update bundles.
10. A component's price changing does not change the bundle's price.
11. Deleting a product or variant that is used in a bundle is blocked, with an error naming every bundle that uses it. Once it has been removed from those bundles, it can be deleted normally.
12. Past orders that include a bundle keep working (viewing, fulfilling and returning) after the bundle is edited or deleted.
13. Upgrading needs no data migration. Existing products, inventory kits and orders behave exactly as before.

## Out of Scope
- Bundles inside bundles
- Bundles built by the shopper ("pick any 3")
- A dedicated bundles page or upsells on component products
- Checkout errors, refund shares and returns (see the checkout and returns issue)
- Admin UI (see the admin bundle screens issue)

## Open Questions
- Is there a maximum number of components per bundle, or is the minimum of 2 the only limit?
- Should deleting the bundle itself be blocked while it has unfulfilled orders, or is that already safe because orders keep a copy of their line items?

===== packages/medusa/src/api/admin/bundles/route.ts
import { createBundleWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
  refetchEntity,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  remapKeysForProduct,
  remapProductResponse,
} from "../products/helpers"
import { AdminCreateBundleType } from "./validators"

/**
 * POST /admin/bundles
 * Creates a bundle: a product with its own prices that is made of several
 * component variants.
 */
export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<
    AdminCreateBundleType,
    HttpTypes.SelectParams
  >,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminProductResponse>
) => {
  // The body was already validated by the middleware (shape, min 2 components,
  // quantities, prices). The workflow validates against the database.
  const { result } = await createBundleWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input: { bundle: req.validatedBody as any },
  })

  // Read the product back with the fields the caller asked for.
  const product = await refetchEntity({
    entity: "product",
    idOrFilter: result.id,
    scope: req.scope,
    fields: remapKeysForProduct(req.queryConfig.fields ?? []),
  })

  res.status(200).json({ product: remapProductResponse(product) })
}

import { updateBundleWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
  refetchEntity,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  remapKeysForProduct,
  remapProductResponse,
} from "../../products/helpers"
import { AdminUpdateBundleType } from "../validators"

/**
 * POST /admin/bundles/:id
 * Updates a bundle's product fields, components, quantities and prices.
 */
export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<
    AdminUpdateBundleType,
    HttpTypes.SelectParams
  >,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminProductResponse>
) => {
  await updateBundleWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input: { id: req.params.id, update: req.validatedBody as any },
  })

  // Read the product back with the fields the caller asked for.
  const product = await refetchEntity({
    entity: "product",
    idOrFilter: req.params.id,
    scope: req.scope,
    fields: remapKeysForProduct(req.queryConfig.fields ?? []),
  })

  res.status(200).json({ product: remapProductResponse(product) })
}

import { z } from "zod"
import {
  AdminGetProductParams,
  CreateProduct,
  UpdateProduct,
} from "../products/validators"

/**
 * Query params for the bundle routes. A bundle is a product, so we accept the
 * same `fields` selection as the product routes.
 */
export const AdminGetBundleParams = AdminGetProductParams

/**
 * One component of a bundle: a variant and how many of it are in one bundle.
 * Quantity must be a whole number of at least 1 (AC 7: "quantity is 0 or less").
 * The remaining rules (existence, inventory tracking, duplicates, no nested
 * bundles) need the database and are checked in the workflow.
 */
const BundleComponent = z
  .object({
    variant_id: z.string(),
    quantity: z.number().int().min(1),
  })
  .strict()

// Bundles have at least 2 components (AC 7).
const BundleComponents = z.array(BundleComponent).min(2)

/**
 * The bundle's own price for a currency. Negative or missing amounts are
 * rejected (AC 7: "a price is missing or negative").
 */
const BundlePrice = z.object({
  currency_code: z.string(),
  amount: z.number().min(0),
  min_quantity: z.number().nullish(),
  max_quantity: z.number().nullish(),
  rules: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional(),
})

// At least one price is required, otherwise the bundle can't be bought.
const BundlePrices = z.array(BundlePrice).min(1)

export type AdminCreateBundleType = z.infer<typeof AdminCreateBundle>
/**
 * Create body: the normal product fields (title, description, images,
 * categories, ...) plus `components` and `prices`. `variants` and `options` are
 * not accepted because the workflow creates the single bundle variant itself.
 */
export const AdminCreateBundle = CreateProduct.omit({
  variants: true,
  options: true,
}).extend({
  components: BundleComponents,
  prices: BundlePrices,
})

export type AdminUpdateBundleType = z.infer<typeof AdminUpdateBundle>
/**
 * Update body: any product field, and optionally new `components` / `prices`.
 */
export const AdminUpdateBundle = UpdateProduct.omit({
  variants: true,
  options: true,
}).extend({
  components: BundleComponents.optional(),
  prices: BundlePrices.optional(),
})

import {
  validateAndTransformBody,
  validateAndTransformQuery,
} from "@medusajs/framework"
import { MiddlewareRoute } from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import { PolicyOperation } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import * as ProductQueryConfig from "../products/query-config"
import { Entities } from "../products/query-config"
import { AdminCreateBundle, AdminGetBundleParams, AdminUpdateBundle } from "./validators"

/**
 * Bundle routes live under /admin/bundles. Like every /admin route they are
 * only available to logged-in admin users (unauthenticated calls get a 401).
 * A bundle is a product, so the product entity policies apply.
 */
export const adminBundleRoutesMiddlewares: MiddlewareRoute[] = [
  {
    method: ["POST"],
    matcher: "/admin/bundles",
    middlewares: [
      validateAndTransformBody(AdminCreateBundle),
      validateAndTransformQuery(
        AdminGetBundleParams,
        ProductQueryConfig.retrieveProductQueryConfig
      ),
    ],
    policies: [{ resource: Entities.product, operation: PolicyOperation.create }],
  },
  {
    method: ["POST"],
    matcher: "/admin/bundles/:id",
    middlewares: [
      validateAndTransformBody(AdminUpdateBundle),
      validateAndTransformQuery(
        AdminGetBundleParams,
        ProductQueryConfig.retrieveProductQueryConfig
      ),
    ],
    policies: [{ resource: Entities.product, operation: PolicyOperation.update }],
  },
]

===== packages/core/core-flows/src/product/utils/bundle.ts
import { MedusaError } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"

/**
 * Bundles (issue #112) are stored without any new data model:
 *
 * - A bundle is a normal product with ONE variant that has its own prices.
 * - The bundle variant is linked (the existing inventory-kit link, which carries
 *   `required_quantity`) to the inventory items of every component. Because of
 *   that, reservations and availability already work per component with no
 *   changes to the cart or inventory code.
 * - The list of components (variant + quantity) is kept in
 *   `product.metadata.bundle.components`. We need it because the merged inventory
 *   links alone can't be turned back into "variant X, quantity N".
 *
 * Everything in this file is a pure function (no container access) so it can be
 * unit tested directly.
 */

/**
 * Key inside `product.metadata` that marks a product as a bundle.
 * Only the bundle workflows are allowed to write it.
 */
export const BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY = "bundle"

/**
 * One component of a bundle as sent by the client.
 */
export type BundleComponentInput = {
  variant_id: string
  quantity: number
}

/**
 * A component variant after it was loaded from the database. Only the fields the
 * validation needs are included.
 */
export type BundleComponentVariant = {
  id: string
  manage_inventory?: boolean | null
  product?: { id?: string; metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null } | null
  inventory_items?:
    | { inventory_item_id: string; required_quantity: number }[]
    | null
}

/**
 * An inventory item link that the bundle variant needs.
 */
export type BundleInventoryLink = {
  inventory_item_id: string
  required_quantity: number
}

/**
 * Smallest number of components a bundle can have.
 */
export const MIN_BUNDLE_COMPONENTS = 2

/**
 * Returns true when the product metadata marks the product as a bundle.
 */
export function isBundleMetadata(
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
): boolean {
  return getBundleComponents(metadata) !== null
}

/**
 * Reads the component list from the product metadata.
 * Returns `null` when the product is not a bundle.
 */
export function getBundleComponents(
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
): BundleComponentInput[] | null {
  const bundle = metadata?.[BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY] as
    | { components?: BundleComponentInput[] }
    | undefined

  if (!bundle || !Array.isArray(bundle.components)) {
    return null
  }

  return bundle.components
}

/**
 * Checks the components of a bundle and throws a `MedusaError` with a clear
 * message for the first problem found. This is the single place for the rules of
 * issue #112 acceptance criterion 7.
 *
 * @param components - what the client sent
 * @param variants - the component variants loaded from the database
 */
export function validateBundleComponents(
  components: BundleComponentInput[],
  variants: BundleComponentVariant[]
): void {
  // Fewer than 2 components is not a bundle.
  if (!components || components.length < MIN_BUNDLE_COMPONENTS) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
      `A bundle needs at least ${MIN_BUNDLE_COMPONENTS} components.`
    )
  }

  // The same variant can't be listed twice (use a larger quantity instead).
  const seen = new Set<string>()
  const duplicates = new Set<string>()
  for (const component of components) {
    if (seen.has(component.variant_id)) {
      duplicates.add(component.variant_id)
    }
    seen.add(component.variant_id)
  }
  if (duplicates.size) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
      `Bundle components must be unique. Variants listed more than once: ${[
        ...duplicates,
      ].join(", ")}. Use the quantity field instead.`
    )
  }

  // Quantities must be whole numbers of at least 1.
  const badQuantity = components.filter(
    (component) =>
      !Number.isInteger(component.quantity) || component.quantity <= 0
  )
  if (badQuantity.length) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
      `Bundle component quantity must be a whole number greater than 0. Invalid for variants: ${badQuantity
        .map((component) => component.variant_id)
        .join(", ")}.`
    )
  }

  // Every component variant has to exist.
  const variantsById = new Map(variants.map((variant) => [variant.id, variant]))
  const missing = components
    .map((component) => component.variant_id)
    .filter((id) => !variantsById.has(id))
  if (missing.length) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
      `Bundle component variants were not found: ${missing.join(", ")}.`
    )
  }

  for (const component of components) {
    const variant = variantsById.get(component.variant_id)!

    // Stock for a bundle is derived from the stock of its components, so a
    // component that doesn't track inventory can't take part.
    if (!variant.manage_inventory || !variant.inventory_items?.length) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
        `Variant ${variant.id} can't be a bundle component because it doesn't track inventory.`
      )
    }

    // Bundles inside bundles are out of scope.
    if (isBundleMetadata(variant.product?.metadata)) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
        `Variant ${variant.id} can't be a bundle component because it belongs to a bundle.`
      )
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Works out which inventory items the bundle variant must be linked to.
 *
 * For each component, its variant's inventory links are copied with
 * `required_quantity = component quantity * the link's own required_quantity`.
 * If two components share an inventory item, the amounts are added together.
 *
 * Example: 2x lens (lens uses 1 item "L") + 1x kit (uses 3 of "L")
 * gives one link "L" with required_quantity 5.
 */
export function buildBundleInventoryLinks(
  components: BundleComponentInput[],
  variants: BundleComponentVariant[]
): BundleInventoryLink[] {
  const variantsById = new Map(variants.map((variant) => [variant.id, variant]))
  const merged = new Map<string, number>()

  for (const component of components) {
    const variant = variantsById.get(component.variant_id)

    for (const link of variant?.inventory_items ?? []) {
      merged.set(
        link.inventory_item_id,
        (merged.get(link.inventory_item_id) ?? 0) +
          component.quantity * link.required_quantity
      )
    }
  }

  return [...merged.entries()].map(([inventory_item_id, required_quantity]) => ({
    inventory_item_id,
    required_quantity,
  }))
}

/**
 * Finds the bundles that use any of the given variants as a component.
 *
 * @param bundles - every bundle product (id, title, metadata)
 * @param variantIds - the variants that are about to be deleted
 * @param ignoreBundleIds - bundles that are being deleted in the same request,
 *   which must not block themselves
 */
export function findBundlesUsingVariants(
  bundles: {
    id: string
    title?: string | null
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
  }[],
  variantIds: string[],
  ignoreBundleIds: string[] = []
): { id: string; title?: string | null }[] {
  const targets = new Set(variantIds)
  const ignored = new Set(ignoreBundleIds)

  return bundles
    .filter((bundle) => !ignored.has(bundle.id))
    .filter((bundle) =>
      (getBundleComponents(bundle.metadata) ?? []).some((component) =>
        targets.has(component.variant_id)
      )
    )
    .map(({ id, title }) => ({ id, title }))
}

/**
 * Throws when the given variants are used by one or more bundles. The error
 * names every bundle so the admin knows what to edit first (AC 11).
 */
export function assertNoBundleUsesVariants(
  bundles: {
    id: string
    title?: string | null
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
  }[],
  variantIds: string[],
  ignoreBundleIds: string[] = []
): void {
  const usedBy = findBundlesUsingVariants(bundles, variantIds, ignoreBundleIds)

  if (usedBy.length) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
      `Cannot delete because it is used in the bundle(s): ${usedBy
        .map((bundle) => `"${bundle.title}" (${bundle.id})`)
        .join(", ")}. Remove it from those bundles first.`
    )
  }
}

/*
 * Protection of existing bundles from the PLAIN product routes.
 *
 * The bundle workflows assume a bundle product has exactly one variant (the one
 * linked to the component inventory items) and that `metadata.bundle` is never
 * lost. The plain product and variant routes know nothing about bundles, so the
 * functions below let the shared workflows protect them.
 */

/**
 * True when a metadata value in an update request would replace ALL metadata
 * instead of being merged: `null` or an empty object. The base service only
 * merges metadata that is non-empty, so these two erase what is stored.
 */
export function isEmptyMetadataUpdate(metadata: unknown): boolean {
  return (
    metadata === null ||
    (typeof metadata === "object" &&
      metadata !== undefined &&
      Object.keys(metadata as object).length === 0)
  )
}

/**
 * Makes a plain product update safe for an existing bundle.
 *
 * - A `null` or `{}` metadata value is dropped, so it doesn't erase the bundle
 *   marker. (Other keys are still merged by the base service, and a key can be
 *   removed by setting it to an empty string, as for any product.)
 * - Variants without an `id` would create a second variant, so the update is
 *   rejected.
 *
 * Returns a copy; the input is not modified.
 *
 * @param update - one product's update data
 * @param bundle - the existing bundle the update targets
 */
export function protectBundleUpdate<T extends Record<string, any>>(
  update: T,
  bundle: { id: string; title?: string | null }
): T {
  const variants = update.variants as { id?: string }[] | null | undefined

  if (variants?.some((variant) => !variant.id)) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
      `A variant can't be added to the bundle "${bundle.title}" (${bundle.id}). A bundle has exactly one variant.`
    )
  }

  // `mergeMetadata` deletes a key whose value is "" (and a null value would
  // overwrite it), so naming the marker key with an empty value removes it.
  // The HTTP validator already blocks the key, this protects direct workflow
  // calls too. Setting real components is how the bundle workflows write it.
  const metadata = update.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined
  if (
    metadata &&
    typeof metadata === "object" &&
    BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY in metadata &&
    (metadata[BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY] === "" ||
      metadata[BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY] === null ||
      metadata[BUNDLE_METADATA_KEY] === undefined)
  ) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
      `The bundle marker of "${bundle.title}" (${bundle.id}) can't be removed. Delete the bundle instead.`
    )
  }

  if (update.metadata !== undefined && isEmptyMetadataUpdate(update.metadata)) {
    const { metadata: _dropped, ...rest } = update
    return rest as T
  }

  return update
}

/**
 * Throws when creating variants would give a bundle more than one variant.
 * Creating a bundle itself is allowed: its product has no variants yet when its
 * single variant is created.
 *
 * @param products - the products the variants are created for (with their
 *   current variant count)
 * @param newVariantsByProduct - how many variants the request adds per product
 */
export function assertBundleKeepsSingleVariant(
  products: {
    id: string
    title?: string | null
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
    variantCount: number
  }[],
  newVariantsByProduct: Record<string, number>
): void {
  for (const product of products) {
    if (!isBundleMetadata(product.metadata)) {
      continue
    }

    if (product.variantCount + (newVariantsByProduct[product.id] ?? 0) > 1) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
        `A variant can't be added to the bundle "${product.title}" (${product.id}). A bundle has exactly one variant.`
      )
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Throws when any of the variants belongs to a bundle. Deleting a bundle's
 * variant would leave a bundle without a variant; delete the bundle instead.
 */
export function assertNoBundleVariants(
  variants: {
    id: string
    product?: {
      id: string
      title?: string | null
      metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
    } | null
  }[]
): void {
  const bundles = new Map<string, string | null | undefined>()

  for (const variant of variants) {
    if (variant.product && isBundleMetadata(variant.product.metadata)) {
      bundles.set(variant.product.id, variant.product.title)
    }
  }

  if (bundles.size) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED,
      `A variant of a bundle can't be deleted: ${[...bundles.entries()]
        .map(([id, title]) => `"${title}" (${id})`)
        .join(", ")}. Delete the bundle instead.`
    )
  }
}

/**
 * Returns the id of a bundle's one variant. Throws if the bundle doesn't have
 * exactly one, instead of silently picking the wrong variant.
 */
export function getBundleVariantId(product: {
  id: string
  variants?: { id: string }[] | null
}): string {
  if (product.variants?.length !== 1) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
      `Bundle ${product.id} has ${
        product.variants?.length ?? 0
      } variants but must have exactly 1.`
    )
  }

  return product.variants[0].id
}
===== packages/core/core-flows/src/product/steps/validate-no-bundle-usage.ts
import { ContainerRegistrationKeys } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { StepResponse, createStep } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { assertNoBundleUsesVariants } from "../utils/bundle"

/**
 * The variants that are about to be deleted.
 */
export type ValidateNoBundleUsageStepInput = {
  /**
   * Variants about to be deleted (directly, or because their product is).
   */
  variant_ids: string[]
  /**
   * Bundle products that are deleted in the same request. They are allowed to
   * go away together with their components.
   */
  ignore_product_ids?: string[]
}

// Products are read in pages so a large catalog doesn't load in one query.
const PAGE_SIZE = 500

export const validateNoBundleUsageStepId = "validate-no-bundle-usage"
/**
 * This step blocks the deletion of a product or variant that is a component of
 * a bundle. It throws a `NOT_ALLOWED` error naming every bundle that uses it.
 * Run it BEFORE anything is deleted. It makes no changes, so it has no
 * compensation.
 */
export const validateNoBundleUsageStep = createStep(
  validateNoBundleUsageStepId,
  async (input: ValidateNoBundleUsageStepInput, { container }) => {
    if (!input.variant_ids?.length) {
      return new StepResponse(void 0)
    }

    const query = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.QUERY)

    // Bundles keep their components in product.metadata, which can't be
    // searched by variant id in the database, so we read the products' metadata
    // page by page and check it in memory.
    // This is fine at current catalog sizes; if it becomes slow, a dedicated
    // link between bundle and component variant would allow a direct lookup.
    let skip = 0
    for (;;) {
      const { data: products } = await query.graph({
        entity: "product",
        fields: ["id", "title", "metadata"],
        pagination: { skip, take: PAGE_SIZE, order: { id: "ASC" } },
      })

      // Throws NOT_ALLOWED listing the bundles when any uses the variants.
      assertNoBundleUsesVariants(
        products as any,
        input.variant_ids,
        input.ignore_product_ids
      )

      if (products.length < PAGE_SIZE) {
        break
      }
      skip += PAGE_SIZE
    }

    return new StepResponse(void 0)
  }
)

import {
  ContainerRegistrationKeys,
  MedusaError,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { StepResponse, createStep } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import {
  BundleComponentInput,
  BundleInventoryLink,
  getBundleComponents,
  getBundleVariantId,
} from "../utils/bundle"

export type LoadBundleStepInput = {
  /**
   * The ID of the bundle product.
   */
  id: string
}

export const loadBundleStepId = "load-bundle"
/**
 * This step loads an existing bundle: its single variant, its current
 * components and its current inventory links. It throws when the product
 * doesn't exist or isn't a bundle. It makes no changes.
 */
export const loadBundleStep = createStep(
  loadBundleStepId,
  async (input: LoadBundleStepInput, { container }) => {
    const query = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.QUERY)

    const { data } = await query.graph({
      entity: "product",
      fields: [
        "id",
        "metadata",
        "variants.id",
        "variants.inventory_items.inventory_item_id",
        "variants.inventory_items.required_quantity",
      ],
      filters: { id: input.id },
    })

    const product = data[0]
    if (!product) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
        `Bundle with id: ${input.id} was not found`
      )
    }

    const components = getBundleComponents(product.metadata)
    if (!components) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
        `Product with id: ${input.id} is not a bundle`
      )
    }

    // A bundle must have exactly one variant. Fail loudly instead of assuming
    // the first one is the right one (older data or direct module calls could
    // have given it more).
    const variantId = getBundleVariantId(product as any)
    const variant = product.variants!.find((v: any) => v.id === variantId)!

    return new StepResponse({
      product_id: product.id as string,
      variant_id: variantId,
      components: components as BundleComponentInput[],
      links: (variant.inventory_items ?? []).map((link: any) => ({
        inventory_item_id: link.inventory_item_id,
        required_quantity: link.required_quantity,
      })) as BundleInventoryLink[],
    })
  }
)

import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { RouteFocusModal } from "../../../components/modals"
import { useRegions } from "../../../hooks/api"
import { usePricePreferences } from "../../../hooks/api/price-preferences"
import { useSalesChannel } from "../../../hooks/api/sales-channels"
import { useStore } from "../../../hooks/api/store"
import { ProductCreateForm } from "./components/product-create-form/product-create-form"

export const ProductCreate = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  const {
    store,
    isPending: isStorePending,
    isError: isStoreError,
    error: storeError,
  } = useStore({
    fields: "+default_sales_channel",
  })

  const {
    sales_channel,
    isPending: isSalesChannelPending,
    isError: isSalesChannelError,
    error: salesChannelError,
  } = useSalesChannel(store?.default_sales_channel_id!, {
    enabled: !!store?.default_sales_channel_id,
  })

  const {
    regions,
    isPending: isRegionsPending,
    isError: isRegionsError,
    error: regionsError,
  } = useRegions({ limit: 9999 })

  const {
    price_preferences,
    isPending: isPricePreferencesPending,
    isError: isPricePreferencesError,
    error: pricePreferencesError,
  } = usePricePreferences({
    limit: 9999,
  })

  const ready =
    !!store &&
    !isStorePending &&
    !!regions &&
    !isRegionsPending &&
    !!sales_channel &&
    !isSalesChannelPending &&
    !!price_preferences &&
    !isPricePreferencesPending

  if (isStoreError) {
    throw storeError
  }

  if (isRegionsError) {
    throw regionsError
  }

  if (isSalesChannelError) {
    throw salesChannelError
  }

  if (isPricePreferencesError) {
    throw pricePreferencesError
  }

  return (
    <RouteFocusModal>
      <RouteFocusModal.Title asChild>
        <span className="sr-only">{t("products.create.title")}</span>
      </RouteFocusModal.Title>
      <RouteFocusModal.Description asChild>
        <span className="sr-only">{t("products.create.description")}</span>
      </RouteFocusModal.Description>
      {ready && (
        <ProductCreateForm
          defaultChannel={sales_channel}
          store={store}
          pricePreferences={price_preferences}
          regions={regions}
        />
      )}
    </RouteFocusModal>
  )
}

import { AdminFile, HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
import { Button, ProgressStatus, ProgressTabs, toast } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react"
import { useWatch } from "react-hook-form"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import {
  RouteFocusModal,
  useRouteModal,
} from "../../../../../components/modals"
import { KeyboundForm } from "../../../../../components/utilities/keybound-form"
import { useExtendableForm } from "../../../../../dashboard-app/forms/hooks"
import { useCreateProduct } from "../../../../../hooks/api/products"
import { sdk } from "../../../../../lib/client"
import { useExtension } from "../../../../../providers/extension-provider"
import {
  PRODUCT_CREATE_FORM_DEFAULTS,
  ProductCreateSchema,
} from "../../constants"
import { normalizeProductFormValues } from "../../utils"
import { ProductCreateDetailsForm } from "../product-create-details-form"
import { ProductCreateInventoryKitForm } from "../product-create-inventory-kit-form"
import { ProductCreateOrganizeForm } from "../product-create-organize-form"
import { ProductCreateVariantsForm } from "../product-create-variants-form"
import { useDocumentDirection } from "../../../../../hooks/use-document-direction"

enum Tab {
  DETAILS = "details",
  ORGANIZE = "organize",
  VARIANTS = "variants",
  INVENTORY = "inventory",
}

type TabState = Record<Tab, ProgressStatus>

const SAVE_DRAFT_BUTTON = "save-draft-button"

type ProductCreateFormProps = {
  defaultChannel?: HttpTypes.AdminSalesChannel
  regions: HttpTypes.AdminRegion[]
  store: HttpTypes.AdminStore
  pricePreferences: HttpTypes.AdminPricePreference[]
}

export const ProductCreateForm = ({
  defaultChannel,
  regions,
  store,
  pricePreferences,
}: ProductCreateFormProps) => {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState<Tab>(Tab.DETAILS)
  const [tabState, setTabState] = useState<TabState>({
    [Tab.DETAILS]: "in-progress",
    [Tab.ORGANIZE]: "not-started",
    [Tab.VARIANTS]: "not-started",
    [Tab.INVENTORY]: "not-started",
  })

  const { t } = useTranslation()
  const { handleSuccess } = useRouteModal()
  const { getFormConfigs } = useExtension()
  const configs = getFormConfigs("product", "create")
  const direction = useDocumentDirection()
  const form = useExtendableForm({
    defaultValues: {
      ...PRODUCT_CREATE_FORM_DEFAULTS,
      sales_channels: defaultChannel
        ? [{ id: defaultChannel.id, name: defaultChannel.name }]
        : [],
    },
    schema: ProductCreateSchema,
    configs,
  })

  const { mutateAsync, isPending } = useCreateProduct()

  const regionsCurrencyMap = useMemo(() => {
    if (!regions?.length) {
      return {}
    }

    return regions.reduce((acc, reg) => {
      acc[reg.id] = reg.currency_code
      return acc
    }, {} as Record<string, string>)
  }, [regions])

  /**
   * TODO: Important to revisit this - use variants watch so high in the tree can cause needless rerenders of the entire page
   * which is suboptimal when rerenders are caused by bulk editor changes
   */

  const watchedVariants = useWatch({
    control: form.control,
    name: "variants",
  })

  const showInventoryTab = useMemo(
    () => watchedVariants.some((v) => v.manage_inventory && v.inventory_kit),
    [watchedVariants]
  )

  const handleSubmit = form.handleSubmit(async (values, e) => {
    let isDraftSubmission = false
    if (e?.nativeEvent instanceof SubmitEvent) {
      const submitter = e?.nativeEvent?.submitter as HTMLButtonElement
      isDraftSubmission = submitter.dataset.name === SAVE_DRAFT_BUTTON
    }

    const media = values.media || []
    const payload = { ...values, media: undefined }

    let uploadedMedia: {
      id?: string
      url: string
      isThumbnail: boolean
      file: File
    }[] = []
    try {
      if (media.length) {
        const thumbnailReq = media.find((m) => m.isThumbnail)
        const otherMediaReq = media.filter((m) => !m.isThumbnail)

        const fileReqs = [] as Promise<
          (AdminFile & {
            isThumbnail: boolean
          })[]
        >[]
        if (thumbnailReq) {
          fileReqs.push(
            sdk.admin.upload
              .create({ files: [thumbnailReq.file] })
              .then((r) => r.files.map((f) => ({ ...f, isThumbnail: true })))
          )
        }
        if (otherMediaReq?.length) {
          fileReqs.push(
            sdk.admin.upload
              .create({
                files: otherMediaReq.map((m) => m.file),
              })
              .then((r) => r.files.map((f) => ({ ...f, isThumbnail: false })))
          )
        }

        uploadedMedia = (await Promise.all(fileReqs)).flat() as {
          id?: string
          url: string
          isThumbnail: boolean
          file: File
        }[]
      }
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof Error) {
        toast.error(error.message)
      }
    }

    await mutateAsync(
      normalizeProductFormValues({
        ...payload,
        media: uploadedMedia,
        status: (isDraftSubmission ? "draft" : "published") as any,
        regionsCurrencyMap,
      }),
      {
        onSuccess: (data) => {
          toast.success(
            t("products.create.successToast", {
              title: data.product.title,
            })
          )

          handleSuccess(`../${data.product.id}`)
        },
        onError: (error) => {
          toast.error(error.message)
        },
      }
    )
  })

  const onNext = async (currentTab: Tab) => {
    const valid = await form.trigger()

    if (!valid) {
      return
    }

    if (currentTab === Tab.DETAILS) {
      setTab(Tab.ORGANIZE)
    }

    if (currentTab === Tab.ORGANIZE) {
      setTab(Tab.VARIANTS)
    }

    if (currentTab === Tab.VARIANTS) {
      setTab(Tab.INVENTORY)
    }
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    const currentState = { ...tabState }
    if (tab === Tab.DETAILS) {
      currentState[Tab.DETAILS] = "in-progress"
    }
    if (tab === Tab.ORGANIZE) {
      currentState[Tab.DETAILS] = "completed"
      currentState[Tab.ORGANIZE] = "in-progress"
    }
    if (tab === Tab.VARIANTS) {
      currentState[Tab.DETAILS] = "completed"
      currentState[Tab.ORGANIZE] = "completed"
      currentState[Tab.VARIANTS] = "in-progress"
    }
    if (tab === Tab.INVENTORY) {
      currentState[Tab.DETAILS] = "completed"
      currentState[Tab.ORGANIZE] = "completed"
      currentState[Tab.VARIANTS] = "completed"
      currentState[Tab.INVENTORY] = "in-progress"
    }

    setTabState({ ...currentState })
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps -- we only want this effect to run when the tab changes
  }, [tab])

  return (
    <RouteFocusModal.Form form={form}>
      <KeyboundForm
        onKeyDown={(e) => {
          // We want to continue to the next tab on enter instead of saving as draft immediately
          if (e.key === "Enter") {
            if (
              e.target instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement &&
              !(e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey)
            ) {
              return
            }

            e.preventDefault()

            if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) {
              if (tab !== Tab.VARIANTS) {
                e.preventDefault()
                e.stopPropagation()
                onNext(tab)

                return
              }

              handleSubmit()
            }
          }
        }}
        onSubmit={handleSubmit}
        className="flex h-full flex-col"
      >
        <ProgressTabs
          dir={direction}
          value={tab}
          onValueChange={async (tab) => {
            const valid = await form.trigger()

            if (!valid) {
              return
            }

            setTab(tab as Tab)
          }}
          className="flex h-full flex-col overflow-hidden"
        >
          <RouteFocusModal.Header>
            <div className="-my-2 w-full border-l">
              <ProgressTabs.List className="justify-start-start flex w-full items-center">
                <ProgressTabs.Trigger
                  status={tabState[Tab.DETAILS]}
                  value={Tab.DETAILS}
                  className="max-w-[200px] truncate"
                >
                  {t("products.create.tabs.details")}
                </ProgressTabs.Trigger>
                <ProgressTabs.Trigger
                  status={tabState[Tab.ORGANIZE]}
                  value={Tab.ORGANIZE}
                  className="max-w-[200px] truncate"
                >
                  {t("products.create.tabs.organize")}
                </ProgressTabs.Trigger>
                <ProgressTabs.Trigger
                  status={tabState[Tab.VARIANTS]}
                  value={Tab.VARIANTS}
                  className="max-w-[200px] truncate"
                >
                  {t("products.create.tabs.variants")}
                </ProgressTabs.Trigger>
                {showInventoryTab && (
                  <ProgressTabs.Trigger
                    status={tabState[Tab.INVENTORY]}
                    value={Tab.INVENTORY}
                    className="max-w-[200px] truncate"
                  >
                    {t("products.create.tabs.inventory")}
                  </ProgressTabs.Trigger>
                )}
              </ProgressTabs.List>
            </div>
          </RouteFocusModal.Header>
          <RouteFocusModal.Body className="size-full overflow-hidden">
            <ProgressTabs.Content
              className="size-full overflow-y-auto"
              value={Tab.DETAILS}
            >
              <ProductCreateDetailsForm form={form} />
            </ProgressTabs.Content>
            <ProgressTabs.Content
              className="size-full overflow-y-auto"
              value={Tab.ORGANIZE}
            >
              <ProductCreateOrganizeForm form={form} />
            </ProgressTabs.Content>
            <ProgressTabs.Content
              className="size-full overflow-y-auto"
              value={Tab.VARIANTS}
            >
              <ProductCreateVariantsForm
                form={form}
                store={store}
                regions={regions}
                pricePreferences={pricePreferences}
              />
            </ProgressTabs.Content>
            {showInventoryTab && (
              <ProgressTabs.Content
                className="size-full overflow-y-auto"
                value={Tab.INVENTORY}
              >
                <ProductCreateInventoryKitForm form={form} />
              </ProgressTabs.Content>
            )}
          </RouteFocusModal.Body>
        </ProgressTabs>
        <RouteFocusModal.Footer>
          <div className="flex items-center justify-end gap-x-2">
            <RouteFocusModal.Close asChild>
              <Button variant="secondary" size="small">
                {t("actions.cancel")}
              </Button>
            </RouteFocusModal.Close>
            <Button
              data-name={SAVE_DRAFT_BUTTON}
              size="small"
              type="submit"
              isLoading={isPending}
              className="whitespace-nowrap"
            >
              {t("actions.saveAsDraft")}
            </Button>
            <PrimaryButton
              tab={tab}
              next={onNext}
              isLoading={isPending}
              showInventoryTab={showInventoryTab}
            />
          </div>
        </RouteFocusModal.Footer>
      </KeyboundForm>
    </RouteFocusModal.Form>
  )
}

type PrimaryButtonProps = {
  tab: Tab
  next: (tab: Tab) => void
  isLoading?: boolean
  showInventoryTab: boolean
}

const PrimaryButton = ({
  tab,
  next,
  isLoading,
  showInventoryTab,
}: PrimaryButtonProps) => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  if (
    (tab === Tab.VARIANTS && !showInventoryTab) ||
    (tab === Tab.INVENTORY && showInventoryTab)
  ) {
    return (
      <Button
        data-name="publish-button"
        key="submit-button"
        type="submit"
        variant="primary"
        size="small"
        isLoading={isLoading}
      >
        {t("actions.publish")}
      </Button>
    )
  }

  return (
    <Button
      key="next-button"
      type="button"
      variant="primary"
      size="small"
      onClick={() => next(tab)}
    >
      {t("actions.continue")}
    </Button>
  )
}
