import { TriangleDownMini } from "@medusajs/icons"
import { ReactNode, useState } from "react"

type CollapsibleBreakdownProps = {
  /** The line of text that opens and closes the list. */
  label: string
  children: ReactNode
}

/**
 * The collapsible list shown under an order line. It was the body of
 * `InventoryKitBreakdown`; a bundle line lists its components the same way
 * (issue #114, AC 6), so the markup lives in one place and both use it.
 */
export const CollapsibleBreakdown = ({
  label,
  children,
}: CollapsibleBreakdownProps) => {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <div
        onClick={() => setIsOpen((open) => !open)}
        className="flex cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 border-t border-dashed px-6 py-4"
      >
        <TriangleDownMini
          style={{
            transform: `rotate(${isOpen ? 0 : -90}deg)`,
          }}
        />
        <span className="text-ui-fg-muted txt-small select-none">{label}</span>
      </div>
      {isOpen && (
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-1 px-6 pb-4">{children}</div>
      )}
    </>
  )
}

type BreakdownRowProps = {
  /** The component or inventory item being listed. */
  name: ReactNode
  /** What is shown on the right, usually a quantity. */
  value: ReactNode
}

/**
 * One row of a `CollapsibleBreakdown`: a name on the left, a value on the
 * right, and a dashed line joining them.
 */
export const BreakdownRow = ({ name, value }: BreakdownRowProps) => (
  <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-x-2">
    <div>
      <span className="txt-small text-ui-fg-subtle font-medium">{name}</span>
    </div>
    <div className="relative flex-1">
      <div className="bottom-[calc(50% - 2px)] absolute h-[1px] w-full border-b border-dashed" />
    </div>
    <span className="txt-small text-ui-fg-muted">{value}</span>
  </div>
)

import { AdminOrderLineItem, AdminReturn } from "@medusajs/types"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"

import {
  getOrderLineBundleComponents,
  getReturnedBundleComponentUnits,
} from "../../../../products/common/bundles"
import { BreakdownRow, CollapsibleBreakdown } from "./collapsible-breakdown"

type BundleComponentBreakdownProps = {
  item: AdminOrderLineItem
  returns: AdminReturn[]
}

/**
 * Lists the components of a bundle line item, and how many of each have come
 * back (issue #114, AC 6).
 *
 * The components and their quantities are read from what was saved on the line
 * when the order was placed (issue #113), not from the bundle product, so
 * editing or deleting the bundle later does not change what the order shows.
 */
export const BundleComponentBreakdown = ({
  item,
  returns,
}: BundleComponentBreakdownProps) => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  const components = getOrderLineBundleComponents(item)

  if (!components?.length) {
    return null
  }

  const returned = getReturnedBundleComponentUnits(returns, item.id)

  return (
    <CollapsibleBreakdown
      label={t("orders.summary.bundleComponents", {
        count: components.length,
      })}
    >
      {components.map((component) => {
        const returnedUnits = returned[component.variant_id]

        return (
          <BreakdownRow
            key={component.variant_id}
            name={component.title || component.variant_id}
            value={
              <span className="flex items-center gap-x-2">
                {!!returnedUnits && (
                  <span className="text-ui-fg-subtle">
                    {t("orders.summary.bundleComponentReturned", {
                      count: returnedUnits,
                    })}
                  </span>
                )}
                <span className="tabular-nums">{component.quantity}x</span>
              </span>
            }
          />
        )
      })}
    </CollapsibleBreakdown>
  )
}

// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { cleanup, render, screen } from "@testing-library/react"
import { MemoryRouter } from "react-router-dom"
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"

import { BundleUsageList, resolveBundleUsage } from "./bundle-usage"

vi.mock("react-i18next", () => ({
  useTranslation: () => ({
    t: (key: string) =>
      key === "products.bundles.usage.description"
        ? "Remove it from these bundles first:"
        : key,
  }),
}))

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup()
})

const components = [
  { variant_id: "variant_camera", quantity: 1 },
  { variant_id: "variant_lens", quantity: 1 },
]

const products = [
  {
    id: "prod_kit",
    title: "Camera kit",
    metadata: { bundle: { components } },
  },
  {
    id: "prod_deal",
    title: "Lens deal",
    metadata: {
      bundle: {
        components: [{ variant_id: "variant_lens", quantity: 2 }],
      },
    },
  },
  { id: "prod_lens", title: "Lens", metadata: null },
]

const makeClient = () => ({
  listProducts: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ products }),
  listVariants: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
    variants: [{ id: "variant_lens" }],
  }),
})

const blocked = { code: "bundle_in_use" }

describe("resolveBundleUsage (AC 7)", () => {
  it("names the bundles that use a variant being deleted", async () => {
    const client = makeClient()

    const usage = await resolveBundleUsage({
      error: blocked,
      variantIds: ["variant_lens"],
      client,
    })

    expect(usage).toEqual([
      { id: "prod_kit", title: "Camera kit" },
      { id: "prod_deal", title: "Lens deal" },
    ])
    expect(client.listVariants).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
  })

  it("looks up the variants of a product being deleted", async () => {
    const client = makeClient()

    const usage = await resolveBundleUsage({
      error: blocked,
      productId: "prod_lens",
      client,
    })

    expect(client.listVariants).toHaveBeenCalledWith("prod_lens")
    expect(usage).toEqual([
      { id: "prod_kit", title: "Camera kit" },
      { id: "prod_deal", title: "Lens deal" },
    ])
  })

  it("does not list the bundle being deleted itself", async () => {
    const client = makeClient()
    client.listVariants.mockResolvedValue({ variants: [{ id: "variant_kit" }] })
    client.listProducts.mockResolvedValue({
      products: [
        {
          id: "prod_kit",
          title: "Camera kit",
          metadata: { bundle: { components: [{ variant_id: "variant_kit" }] } },
        },
      ],
    })

    const usage = await resolveBundleUsage({
      error: blocked,
      productId: "prod_kit",
      client,
    })

    expect(usage).toEqual([])
  })

  // Only the tagged error means "a bundle uses this". Anything else keeps the
  // plain message it came with, and costs no extra requests.
  it("ignores a failure that is not about a bundle", async () => {
    const client = makeClient()

    expect(
      await resolveBundleUsage({
        error: { code: "insufficient_inventory" },
        variantIds: ["variant_lens"],
        client,
      })
    ).toBeNull()
    expect(client.listProducts).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
  })

  it("gives up rather than throwing when the lookup fails", async () => {
    const client = makeClient()
    client.listProducts.mockRejectedValue(new Error("network"))

    expect(
      await resolveBundleUsage({
        error: blocked,
        variantIds: ["variant_lens"],
        client,
      })
    ).toBeNull()
  })
})

describe("BundleUsageList (AC 7)", () => {
  it("lists every bundle with a link to it", () => {
    render(
      <MemoryRouter>

```bash
cd /Users/alexgrapsas/medusa-114 && cat > packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/products/common/components/bundle-usage/bundle-usage.tsx <<'EOF'
import { toast } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { Link } from "react-router-dom"

import { sdk } from "../../../../../lib/client"
import { findBundlesUsingVariants, isBundleUsageError } from "../../bundles"

/*
 * Deleting a product or variant that a bundle uses is blocked by the delete
 * workflows (issue #112, AC 11). The dashboard turns that into the list of
 * bundles, each with a link, instead of showing the message as it is
 * (issue #114, AC 7).
 *
 * The error carries a code, not the list, because the HTTP error handler only
 * passes `code`, `type` and `message` through. So the code says this is a
 * bundle conflict, and the bundles are looked up here to get an ID to link to.
 * The lookup only runs when a delete was refused.
 */

/** How many products one lookup page reads. */
const PAGE_SIZE = 200

/** The most pages to read before giving up on a large catalog. */
const MAX_PAGES = 10

type BundleUsageClient = {
  listProducts: (query: {
    fields: string
    limit: number
    offset: number
  }) => Promise<{
    products: {
      id: string
      title?: string | null
      metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null
    }[]
  }>
  listVariants: (productId: string) => Promise<{ variants: { id: string }[] }>
}

/**
 * The real client. It is passed in so the resolver can be tested without the
 * SDK.
 */
export const bundleUsageClient: BundleUsageClient = {
  listProducts: (query) => sdk.admin.product.list(query as any) as any,
  listVariants: (productId) =>
    sdk.admin.product.listVariants(productId, {
      fields: "id",
      limit: 1000,
    }) as any,
}

type ResolveBundleUsageInput = {
  /** The error the delete failed with. */
  error?: { code?: string } | null
  /** The product being deleted, when a whole product was deleted. */
  productId?: string
  /** The variants being deleted, when they are already known. */
  variantIds?: string[]
  client?: BundleUsageClient
}

/**
 * Returns the bundles that blocked a delete, or `null` when the failure was
 * something else and the caller should show its own message.
 *
 * Bundles keep their components in product metadata, which cannot be searched
 * by variant ID, so the products are read in pages and matched in memory. This
 * is the same approach `validateNoBundleUsageStep` takes on the server.
 */
export const resolveBundleUsage = async ({
  error,
  productId,
  variantIds,
  client = bundleUsageClient,
}: ResolveBundleUsageInput): Promise<
  { id: string; title?: string | null }[] | null
> => {
  if (!isBundleUsageError(error)) {
    return null
  }

  try {
    let ids = variantIds ?? []

    if (!ids.length && productId) {
      ids = (await client.listVariants(productId)).variants.map((v) => v.id)
    }

    if (!ids.length) {
      return null
    }

    const found: { id: string; title?: string | null }[] = []

    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
      const { products } = await client.listProducts({
        fields: "id,title,metadata",
        limit: PAGE_SIZE,
        offset: page * PAGE_SIZE,
      })

      found.push(
        ...findBundlesUsingVariants(
          products,
          ids,
          productId ? [productId] : []
        )
      )

      if (products.length < PAGE_SIZE) {
        break
      }
    }

    return found
  } catch {
    // The delete already failed; failing the lookup too should not replace the
    // admin's error with a crash. The caller falls back to the message.
    return null
  }
}

type BundleUsageListProps = {
  bundles: { id: string; title?: string | null }[]
}

/**
 * The bundles that blocked a delete, each linking to its product page.
 */
export const BundleUsageList = ({ bundles }: BundleUsageListProps) => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-y-1">
      <span>{t("products.bundles.usage.description")}</span>
      <ul className="flex flex-col gap-y-0.5">
        {bundles.map((bundle) => (
          <li key={bundle.id}>
            <Link
              to={`/products/${bundle.id}`}
              className="text-ui-fg-interactive"
            >
              {bundle.title || bundle.id}
            </Link>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  )
}

/**
 * How long the blocked-delete toast stays up. It holds links the admin is
 * meant to follow, so it outlasts a normal error toast.
 */
const USAGE_TOAST_DURATION = 30000

/**
 * Shows a failed delete. When bundles blocked it, they are listed with a link
 * to each (AC 7); otherwise the given fallback is shown.
 *
 * @returns whether the failure was a bundle conflict
 */
export const showDeleteError = async (
  input: ResolveBundleUsageInput & {
    header: string
    fallback: { header: string; description?: string }
  }
): Promise<boolean> => {
  const bundles = await resolveBundleUsage(input)

  if (!bundles?.length) {
    toast.error(input.fallback.header, {
      description: input.fallback.description,
    })
    return false
  }

  toast.error(input.header, {
    description: <BundleUsageList bundles={bundles} />,
    duration: USAGE_TOAST_DURATION,
  })

  return true
}

// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { RouteObject } from "react-router-dom"
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"

// The route map imports layouts that pull in the SDK client, which reads these
// bare globals at module load time (see edit-product-form.spec.tsx); Vite
// injects them in the real app.
vi.hoisted(() => {
  const g = global as any
  g.__BACKEND_URL__ = "http://localhost:9000"
  g.__AUTH_TYPE__ = "session"
  g.__JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY__ = ""
})

import { getRouteMap } from "./get-route.map"

/**
 * Returns the first route in the tree whose `path` equals `path`.
 */
const findRoute = (
  routes: RouteObject[],
  path: string
): RouteObject | undefined => {
  for (const route of routes) {
    if (route.path === path) {
      return route
    }

    const found = findRoute(route.children ?? [], path)

    if (found) {
      return found
    }
  }
}

/**
 * The child routes of the product detail page: /products -> :id -> "".
 * Paths like "edit" are used all over the app, so the lookup is scoped here.
 */
const getProductDetailChildren = () => {
  const routes = getRouteMap({ settingsRoutes: [], coreRoutes: [] })

  const products = findRoute(routes, "/products")
  const productId = findRoute(products?.children ?? [], ":id")
  const detail = findRoute(productId?.children ?? [], "")

  return detail?.children ?? []
}

```text
describe("getRouteMap product detail routes", () => {
  // Guards against a bad merge collapsing two child routes into one object
  // (a duplicate `path`/`lazy` key means the last one silently wins, and the
  // other route stops existing).
  it.each(["edit", "duplicate", "edit-all"])(
    "registers /products/:id/%s as its own lazy route",
    (path) => {
      const matches = getProductDetailChildren().filter(
        (route) => route.path === path
      )

      expect(matches).toHaveLength(1)
      expect(matches[0].lazy).toBeTypeOf("function")
    }
  )

  it("keeps duplicate and edit-all as separate sibling routes", () => {
    const children = getProductDetailChildren()
    const duplicate = children.find((route) => route.path === "duplicate")
    const editAll = children.find((route) => route.path === "edit-all")

    expect(duplicate).toBeDefined()
    expect(editAll).toBeDefined()
    expect(duplicate).not.toBe(editAll)
  })
})

      {

      const err: FetchError = await client.fetch<any>("throw").catch((e) => e)
      expect(err.status).toEqual(500)
      expect(err.message).toEqual("Internal Server Error")
    })

    /*
     * The server distinguishes its errors with `type` and `code`; a caller that
     * has to tell one refusal from another can only do it on those. Without
     * them the only thing left is matching on the message text, which changes
     * with wording and translation.
     */
    it("should keep the error type and code the server sent", async () => {

      expect(err.type).toEqual("not_allowed")
      expect(err.code).toEqual("bundle_in_use")
      expect(err.message).toEqual(

      )
    })

      expect(err.code).toBeUndefined()
    })'''

 * passes `code`, `type` and `message` through. So the code says this is a
 * bundle conflict, and the bundles are looked up here to get an ID to link to.
 * The lookup only runs when a delete was refused.

/** How many products one lookup page reads. */

/** The most pages to read before giving up on a large catalog. */

......
import { toast } from "@medusajs/ui"

import { BundleUsageList } from "./bundle-usage-list"
import { ResolveBundleUsageInput, resolveBundleUsage } from "./bundle-usage"

/**
 * How long the blocked-delete toast stays up. It holds links the admin is
 * meant to follow, so it outlasts a normal error toast.
 */
const USAGE_TOAST_DURATION = 30000

/**
 * Shows a failed delete. When bundles blocked it, they are listed with a link
 * to each (AC 7); otherwise the given fallback is shown.
 *
 * @returns whether the failure was a bundle conflict
 */
export const showDeleteError = async (
  input: ResolveBundleUsageInput & {
    header: string
    fallback: { header: string; description?: string }
  }
): Promise<boolean> => {
  const bundles = await resolveBundleUsage(input)

  if (!bundles?.length) {
    toast.error(input.fallback.header, {
      description: input.fallback.description,
    })
    return false
  }

  toast.error(input.header, {
    description: <BundleUsageList bundles={bundles} />,
    duration: USAGE_TOAST_DURATION,
  })

  return true
}

```text
Closes #97

What: Adds a promotion CSV export. The Promotions list has an Export action next to Import. It opens a drawer, and confirming starts a background export of every promotion matching the list's current filters and search. The file uses the promotion import's columns, so an exported file can be imported again.

Why: Promotions could be imported but not exported, so there was no way to review them in a spreadsheet, keep a backup, or move them to another store. My spec review and the answers to the issue's open questions are on #97.

How: It follows the customer export file for file: a step that pages through promotions with an id cursor and streams the CSV to the File Module, a workflow that runs the step in the background and sends a feed notification on success or failure, `POST /admin/promotions/export` returning 202 with a transaction ID, an SDK method, and the Export action on the list.

The one deliberate difference is that the row conversion stays in `export-promotions.ts`, where the first commits on this branch put it, instead of living inside the step as the customer version does. The step imports `normalizePromotionForExport` and `EXPORT_COLUMNS` from there. The columns come from the import's own `COLUMNS` map rather than a second copy of the list, so the two can't drift when a column is added later.

Rules go out in the import's `attribute:operator:value1|value2` form, booleans as `true` and `false`, and anything the promotion doesn't have as an empty cell. A rule with no readable values is left out rather than written in a form the import would reject. The Export link carries the list's query string, which is how the drawer reads the same filters the list is showing.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: the promotions list has an Export action next to Import | `promotion-list-table.spec.tsx > links to the promotion export from the list header` | unit | AC |
| AC2: the export covers every promotion matching the list's filters and search, not only the current page | `promotion-list-table.spec.tsx > forwards the list's filters and search to the export`; `promotion-export.spec.tsx > sends the list's current filters with the export request`; `promotion-export.spec.ts > exports only the promotions matching the search`; `> ignores pagination and exports every matching promotion` | unit, integration | AC |
| AC3: same column headers, in the same order, as the import template | `export-promotions.spec.ts > uses the import template's columns in the template's order`; `promotion-export.spec.ts > exports every promotion using the import template's columns` | unit, integration | AC. The header is a literal in both tests, written from the list in AC3, not read from the code |
| AC4: rules use `attribute:operator:value`, values joined by `\|`, rules by `;` | `export-promotions.spec.ts > joins a rule's values with \| and separate rules with ;`; `> writes the buyget quantities and both rule columns`; `promotion-export.spec.ts > writes each promotion as one row in the import's format` | unit, integration | AC. The expected string is AC4's own worked example |
| AC5: empty fields are empty cells, booleans are `true`/`false` | `export-promotions.spec.ts > flattens a promotion and its application method into one row`; `> leaves a field the promotion doesn't have as an empty cell`; `> writes a limit of 0 and a value of 0 rather than treating them as unset`; `> leaves the code cell empty for a promotion that has no code`; `promotion-export.spec.ts > writes each promotion as one row in the import's format` | unit, integration | AC. The integration test asserts the file's raw text, because the CSV reader coerces `false` and `10` back to a boolean and a number |
| AC6: importing an exported file recreates the promotion, checked with the existing import parser | `export-promotions.spec.ts > recreates a standard promotion with the same settings and rules`; `> recreates a buyget promotion with its quantities and both rule sets`; `> exports every promotion in the file, one row each`; `> leaves out a rule with no attribute or no operator, so the file still imports`; `> leaves out a rule whose only value is blank, so the file still imports` | unit | AC. The expected `CreatePromotionDTO` is written out by hand from the source promotion, not captured from a run. For the last two, the expected result is AC6's own wording: no errors, and the promotion comes back with the rules that were readable |
| AC7: the export runs in the background, the route returns 202 with a `transaction_id`, and a notification carries the download link | `promotion-export.spec.ts`, in the `exportPromotions` helper every test goes through: it asserts the 202, the transaction ID, and the feed notification with the CSV's URL and `text/csv` type | integration | AC |
| AC8: unit tests for the conversion including rule formatting and the round trip, an HTTP integration test for the route and its filters, and a dashboard test for the Export action | All three: `export-promotions.spec.ts` (14 tests), `promotion-export.spec.ts` (5 tests), `promotion-export.spec.tsx` and `promotion-list-table.spec.tsx` (7 tests) | unit, integration | AC |

Not tested automatically, and why: nothing is manual-only. One gap worth naming though: I have not clicked the Export action in a running dashboard, so AC1 and AC2 are covered at the component level by the href and the request the drawer sends, not end to end in a browser.

AI-written tests: the step, workflow, route, drawer and all the tests on this branch were drafted with Claude Code. No expected value was copied from the output of code this PR adds, with one deliberate exception noted under Tech Debt. The headers and rule strings come from AC3 and AC4, the round trip's expected result is written out from the source promotion by hand, and the two exact CSV rows in the integration test were written from AC3's column order plus AC4 and AC5's formatting rules before the test was run; both matched on the first run.

Three of the tests on the export helper came from running a mutation tool over it rather than from reading the ACs again: an empty `Code` cell, a rule missing its attribute or operator, and a rule whose only value is blank. Two of them kill mutants nothing else caught. Dropping the `!rule.attribute` guard from `serializeRules` was failed by only the new rule test, and letting `code` fall through as `undefined` instead of an empty cell was failed by only the new code test. The third overlaps a test that already existed. I checked each by making the change and watching which tests failed.

Two things I had to correct. My first integration assertions expected `Automatic` to be the string `"false"` and `Discount Value` the string `"10"`, and the test failed: `csv2json` coerces those back to a boolean and a number when it reads the file, so a parsed row can never show how a value was written. The test now asserts the raw file text for AC5, which is what the criterion is actually about. Separately, the typecheck caught `useExportPromotions` taking a `query` argument it never used; it now passes it to the SDK the way `useExportCustomers` does.

CI doesn't run on PRs here, so these runs stand in for it.

Failures this branch does add, all in one place: `i18n:validate` reports `Missing required key: "export" at /promotions` for each of the 32 non-English locales, because the schema now requires the key and only `en.json` has it. That is 32 of the 5506 issues the sweep reports; the other 5474 predate this branch. The two exports already merged are in the same position, missing `customers.export` in 32 locales and `orders.export` in 25, so this follows their precedent rather than setting a new one. It is recorded under Tech Debt. Note that the i18n CI job wouldn't catch any of this: `admin-i18n-validation.yml` only validates translation files the PR *adds*, and this one modifies `en.json` and `$schema.json`.

## Tech Debt

Introduced: a rule value containing `;`, `|` or `:` exports fine but reads back as a different rule, because the import splits on those. In practice these values are IDs and currency codes. There's a test pinning the behavior so it's documented rather than discovered, and that is the one expected value taken from existing code rather than an AC, since it records what the import parser does today. The reasoning is in my comment on #97, and fixing it means an escaping scheme on both sides, which is its own issue.

Introduced: the schema now requires `promotions.export`, which only `en.json` has, so `i18n:validate` reports a missing key for each of the 32 other locales. The customer and order exports already do the same thing, and translating 32 locales isn't this issue's job, so I followed them rather than making the key optional for promotions alone. The numbers are above.

Introduced: `useExportPromotions` takes the filters as a hook argument and ignores the payload passed to `mutateAsync`, which is how `useExportCustomers` works. The drawer passes the same value to both, so it behaves correctly, but the mutation's payload type is misleading.

Encountered: `en.json` has `"duplicate": "Duplicate"` twice in the `actions` block, at lines 120 and 147. JSON parsers keep the last one, so nothing is broken, but a round trip through a JSON parser silently drops one. I hit that while adding the export keys and switched to a text insert to leave it alone. It predates this branch.

Encountered: the export is tied to the import's template by design, so a promotion field with no column can't be exported. Usage counts, campaign details and campaign budgets are the ones that come up, and the issue lists them as out of scope.

Encountered: this branch is 16 commits behind develop, including the bundles API and the low-stock dashboard. Nothing it touches overlaps, and the suites above pass, but it should take a merge from develop before it goes in.

cat > ~/csci535-notes/pr-114-description.md <<'MARKDOWN'
Closes #114

What: Adds the admin screens for product bundles. Products gets a "Create bundle" button that opens a form with the normal product fields plus a component picker and the bundle's own price. A bundle's product page lists its components with their quantities and has an "Edit bundle" action that reopens the same form filled in. An order that contains a bundle shows the bundle's components under the line, with the ones that have come back marked as returned. And when deleting a product or variant is blocked because bundles use it, the dashboard lists those bundles with a link to each instead of showing the raw message.

This covers acceptance criteria 1 through 7. Criteria 8, 9 and 10 are the return form, and they are not in this PR: they lean hardest on the single-item return work in #113, which is still open as #117, so building the form against it now would mean rewriting it if that PR changes. They stay on #114 for a follow-up.

Why: #112 added the bundle API and #113 made bundles work through checkout and returns, but a store owner still had to send requests by hand to create one, and nothing in the admin showed that a product was a bundle at all. This is the part that makes the team feature (#101) demoable end to end through the dashboard.

How: Bundles are products, so the screens reuse the product form rather than restating it. `BundleFormFields` renders the product create form's own general, media and organization sections against a `BundleSchema` that declares the same field names, and adds two sections of its own: a component list laid out like the existing inventory kit rows (a variant combobox paired with a quantity) and a price input per store currency. The create and edit forms are the same body with different buttons; `mapBundleToFormValues` fills it from a stored bundle using the full product edit flow's own mapper, and `normalizeBundleFormValues` turns it back into the request using the product form's normalizer with `variants` and `options` dropped. There is a test that round-trips a bundle through both so a field can't be lost in the middle.

The product page section and the order line breakdown read the bundle from where it is already stored rather than fetching it again: `product.metadata.bundle.components` for the product page, and the components saved on the order line when the order was placed for the order page, so editing or deleting a bundle later doesn't change what a past order shows. The order line's collapsible list is the markup that was inside `InventoryKitBreakdown`, pulled out into `CollapsibleBreakdown` so both use one copy.

Three things outside the dashboard were needed to make the screens work. `POST /admin/bundles` had no SDK method, so `sdk.admin.bundle` was added. The error that blocks deleting a component now carries a code (`MedusaError.Codes.BUNDLE_IN_USE`) so the dashboard can recognise it without reading the message text. And `FetchError` in the JS SDK dropped the `type` and `code` the server sends, keeping only `message`, so no caller could branch on an error code at all; it now carries both.

## Design

Decision: "Create bundle" is its own button and its own screen, not a mode inside the product create wizard. Alternatives: a switch on the existing wizard's first tab that hides the options and variants tabs; a choice in a dropdown on the Create button. I went with a separate screen because the two forms post different bodies to different routes and a bundle has no options or variants to build up, so sharing the wizard would mean carrying a branch through all four of its tabs and its tab-state effect. The sections the two forms do share are shared as components instead. This is one of the issue's open questions and I answered it rather than leave the screens unbuildable; it is worth confirming with the customer before Sprint 4.

Decision: the bundle forms use their own react-hook-form resolver instead of `zodResolver`. Alternatives: use `zodResolver` and accept that AC 3 shows nothing; upgrade `@hookform/resolvers` for the whole dashboard. `@hookform/resolvers@3.4.2` predates zod 4: it reads `ZodError.errors`, which zod 4 renamed to `issues`, so it rethrows instead of handing react-hook-form any errors. 116 files call it and 104 render `<Form.ErrorMessage />`, and none of them can display anything, so AC 3 is unreachable with it. The upgrade is the real fix but it touches every form in the dashboard and belongs in #98, not here. `zodFormResolver` is 40 lines, maps zod 4 issues onto the shape react-hook-form reads, and has a test that fails the day the dependency is upgraded so it gets removed then.

Decision: the blocked-delete error is recognised by its code, and the bundles are then looked up in the dashboard to get an ID to link to. Alternatives: parse the bundle titles and IDs out of the error message, which already contains them; change the framework's HTTP error handler to pass structured data through. Parsing the message means the wording of a server error is a contract, which is what went wrong on #58; changing the error handler changes the response shape of every route in the project for one screen. Tagging at the source and matching on the tag is the same approach as `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY` on #58. The lookup pages through products and matches their metadata in memory, which is what `validateNoBundleUsageStep` does on the server, and it only runs when a delete was refused.

Decision: a bundle line on an order shows its components instead of its inventory kit. Alternatives: show both lists; keep only the inventory kit. A bundle's variant is linked to the inventory items of all its components, so it is an inventory kit too and the existing breakdown already appears for one. Both lists say the same thing, once in inventory items and once in variants, and the components are the ones with names, quantities and return state, so they replace it for bundle lines only.

Decision: the quantity input carries no `min` or `step`. Alternative: keep `min={1}` as an affordance. The browser's own constraint validation blocks the submit event before react-hook-form runs, so a quantity of 0 produced a native tooltip rather than the inline message AC 3 asks for, and which one the admin sees depends on the browser. The schema is now the only place the quantity rules live. A test covers 0, a negative, a fraction and an empty input.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: an admin can create a bundle from the product fields, picked variants, quantities and prices | `bundle-create-form.spec.tsx > sends the product fields, the components and the price`, `> saves a bundle as a draft from the same form`; `bundles.spec.ts > sends the components with whole-number quantities`, `> sends a price per currency and leaves blank ones out`, `> sends the product fields the same way the product form does`, `> does not send variants or options, which the bundle route rejects`; `validators.spec.ts > accepts the body the admin bundle create form sends` | unit | AC. The payload is written out from AC1's field list and from the `components`/`prices` shape in #112's own create route, not captured from a run |
| AC2: an admin can edit a bundle's product fields, components, quantities and prices | `bundle-edit-form.spec.tsx > starts from the bundle's own fields, components and price`, `> saves a changed title, quantity and price`, `> saves a component added to the bundle`; `bundles.spec.ts > fills the form with the bundle's components`, `> fills the form with the bundle's prices, keyed by currency or region`, `> fills the product fields the same way the product edit form does`, `> round-trips a bundle through the form and back to a payload`; `validators.spec.ts > accepts the body the admin bundle edit form sends` | unit | AC. The round-trip test's expected payload is the stored bundle it started from, which is what "edit" means; the rest come from AC2 |
| AC3: invalid input shows inline errors and blocks saving (fewer than 2 components, quantity of 0 or less, missing price) | `bundle-form-validation.spec.tsx > shows the minimum-components message and blocks saving`, `> shows a message on the row whose quantity is 0 and blocks saving`, `> shows a message when a quantity is left empty`, `> shows the missing-price message and blocks saving`, `> shows a message on the row whose variant is not picked`, `> shows a message when the same variant is a component twice`, `> clears the message once the quantity is corrected`, `> lets a bundle with two components and a price through`; `bundle-create-form.spec.tsx > does not send anything when the bundle is incomplete`; `bundle-edit-form.spec.tsx > will not save a bundle cut down to one component`; `constants.spec.ts` (15 tests on `BundleSchema`); `zod-form-resolver.spec.ts` (7 tests) | unit | AC. The three rules are AC3's own list. `zod-form-resolver.spec.ts > documents why the stock zodResolver cannot be used here` asserts the current dependency throws, which is the reason the resolver exists |
| AC4: errors from the server are shown, and anything the admin entered is kept | `bundle-create-form.spec.tsx > shows a rejected save and keeps what was entered`; `bundle-edit-form.spec.tsx > shows a rejected save and keeps the edited values` | unit | AC. The two error messages are the real ones from `validateBundleComponents` in core-flows ("belongs to a bundle", "must be unique"), which is the example AC4 gives |
| AC5: a bundle's product page lists its components and their quantities | `product-bundle-section.spec.tsx > lists each component with its quantity`, `> links each component to its own product page`, `> keeps the component listed when its variant cannot be read`, `> renders nothing for a product that is not a bundle`; `bundles.spec.ts > reads the components a bundle stores in its metadata`, `> returns null for a product that is not a bundle`, `> is true only for a product with bundle components` | unit | AC, plus #112's metadata layout for where the components are read from |
| AC6: an order page shows the components of every bundle in the order, including which have been returned | `bundle-component-breakdown.spec.tsx > names the components of the bundle line and how many of each`, `> marks the components that have been returned`, `> does not mark a component returned from another line`, `> renders nothing for a line that is not a bundle`; `bundles.spec.ts > reads the components saved on the order line`, `> adds up what was returned per component of that line`, `> ignores canceled returns`, `> is empty when nothing was returned` | unit | AC. The line and return shapes are #113's: `metadata.bundle.components` on the order line and `metadata.bundle_component` on the return item |
| AC7: a blocked delete lists the bundles that use the product or variant, each with a link, instead of a generic error | `bundle-usage.spec.tsx > names the bundles that use a variant being deleted`, `> looks up the variants of a product being deleted`, `> does not list the bundle being deleted itself`, `> ignores a failure that is not about a bundle`, `> gives up rather than throwing when the lookup fails`, `> lists every bundle with a link to it`, `> falls back to the bundle's id when it has no title`; `bundles.spec.ts > names every bundle that uses the variant`, `> is empty when no bundle uses the variant`, `> leaves out the product being deleted`, and the three `isBundleUsageError` tests; `bundle.spec.ts > tags the error with the bundle-in-use code` (core-flows); `client.spec.ts > should keep the error type and code the server sent`, `> should leave the type and code unset when the server sends none` (js-sdk) | unit | AC. The code string `bundle_in_use` is asserted as a literal on both sides so the tag can't drift; the message the SDK test uses is the one `assertNoBundleUsesVariants` produces |

Not tested automatically, and why: nothing is manual-only, but two gaps are worth naming. I have not clicked these screens in a running dashboard, so every AC is covered at the component level and at the form-to-route boundary rather than in a browser. There is no Playwright or Cypress in this repo, so the seam between the form and the API is pinned instead by two tests that hold the same payload: `bundle-create-form.spec.tsx` asserts the object the form sends, and `validators.spec.ts` in `@medusajs/medusa` asserts the route's real zod validator accepts that object. Separately, AC6's returned-component marking is tested against the return item shape #113 saves, not against a return created by #117, because that PR is not merged.

AI-written tests: the screens and all the tests on this branch were drafted with Claude Code. No expected value was copied from the output of code this PR adds. The messages in the AC3 tests are the English strings from `en.json`, asserted through a stubbed translator so a renamed key fails the test rather than silently passing a key through. The AC4 messages are the real server strings, read out of `validateBundleComponents`. The AC1 and AC2 payloads were written from the ACs and from #112's create route before being run; the first run of the AC1 payload test failed, which is noted below.

Three things I had to correct, all caught by running things rather than reading them. The AC3 quantity tests failed at first with no message rendered: `min={1}` on the input made the browser block the submit event before validation ran, which is a real bug for the criterion and not a test problem, so the attributes came off the input. The AC7 lookup was written to read `error.code` before I checked whether the SDK keeps it; it does not, which is why `FetchError` changed. And the first pass used `zodResolver` like every other form in the dashboard; I only found out it cannot work by calling it directly and watching it throw, which is `zod-form-resolver.spec.ts`'s last test.

## Tech Debt

Introduced: the bundle forms use `zodFormResolver` while the other 116 forms use `zodResolver`, so the dashboard now has two resolvers. That is the only way to meet AC 3 without upgrading `@hookform/resolvers` for everything, which belongs in #98. `zod-form-resolver.spec.ts > documents why the stock zodResolver cannot be used here` fails as soon as the upgrade lands, which is the signal to delete the file and the second resolver with it.

Introduced: AC 7's bundle lookup reads the product list in pages of 200 and matches metadata in memory, up to 10 pages. A catalog with more than 2000 products can have a bundle that blocks a delete and is not named in the list; the admin still gets the message, just not the links. This is the same limit the server-side check has, and fixing it properly means a link between a bundle and its component variants so it can be queried, which is #112's data model and its own issue.

Introduced: the schema now requires four keys that only `en.json` has, so `i18n:validate` reports a missing key for each of the 32 other locales. Numbers are above.

Introduced: prices are per currency only. A region-scoped price round-trips correctly if the bundle already has one (`mapBundleToFormValues` keys it by region ID and `normalizePrices` sends the rule back), but the form shows no input to add one. No AC asks for it; the product form's pricing grid does it and would be the thing to reuse.

Introduced: the three reused product sections are passed the bundle form with a cast, because they are typed against `ProductCreateSchemaType`. `BundleSchema` declares the same name and type for every field they read and leaves out only `options`, `variants` and `enable_variants`, which none of them touch, so the cast is sound today but nothing enforces it. Making those sections generic over the fields they actually use would, and that is a change to the product form.

Encountered: `vite.config.mts` did not define `__MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE__`, one of the six globals the source reads. `file-upload.tsx` reads it as a bare global while its module loads, so the standalone dashboard dev server threw a `ReferenceError` before React mounted and served a blank page, which made these screens impossible to demo at all. I added the define, because without it the feature cannot be shown end to end, which is what #101 is being judged on. It is a dev-server config change and does not alter product behaviour. The bundled admin already defines all six (`admin-bundler/src/utils/config.ts`); this was the last one missing here.

Encountered: `FetchError` in the JS SDK threw away the `type` and `code` the HTTP error handler sends and kept only `message`, so no dashboard code could tell one refusal from another except by matching message text. Fixed here because AC 7 needs it, with two tests in `client.spec.ts`. Anything else in the dashboard that currently matches on a message could now match on the code instead; this PR does not go looking for those.

Encountered: criteria 8, 9 and 10 (the return form) are not implemented. They depend on #117, which is open. The components, their saved refund shares and the returned quantities are already read on this branch for AC 6, so the form has the data it needs when that merges.

Encountered: the issue's second open question, whether the product list should badge or filter bundles, is not answered here. No acceptance criterion covers it, and the product page section plus the "Edit bundle" action are enough to find and change a bundle. It is worth asking the customer before Sprint 4, together with the create-screen question answered under Design.

Here's where things stand. Nothing committed, pushed, or posted.

**Issue #114** — assigned to `angrapsas`, labelled `scope: medium`. That's the only GitHub write I made.

**Worktree** — `~/medusa-114` on `feat/issue-114-bundle-admin-screens`, branched off `origin/feat/issue-113-bundles-checkout-and-returns` as you asked. 55 files, +4818/−100, uncommitted.

## What's there

Criteria 1–7. Criteria 8–10 untouched.

- **Create / edit** — "Create bundle" button on Products opens a one-page form; "Edit bundle" on a bundle's product page reopens it filled in. Both render the product create form's own general, media and organization sections against a `BundleSchema` that declares the same field names, plus a component picker laid out like the existing inventory-kit rows and a price input per store currency. `mapBundleToFormValues` fills it using the full product edit flow's mapper; `normalizeBundleFormValues` sends it back through the product form's normalizer with `variants`/`options` dropped. There's a round-trip test so a field can't go missing in the middle.
- **Inline validation** — works, but not through `zodResolver`. I verified your HANDOFF note by calling it directly: `@hookform/resolvers@3.4.2` reads `ZodError.errors`, which zod 4 renamed to `issues`, so it throws instead of populating form state. AC3 is unreachable with it. The bundle forms use a 40-line `zodFormResolver`; its last test asserts the stock one throws, so it fails the day #98 upgrades the dep and the file gets deleted.
- **Product page / order page** — components read from `product.metadata.bundle.components` and, on orders, from what #113 saved on the line, so editing a bundle later doesn't change a past order. The order breakdown reuses `InventoryKitBreakdown`'s markup, pulled out into `CollapsibleBreakdown`.
- **Blocked deletion** — tagged at source (`MedusaError.Codes.BUNDLE_IN_USE`), matched on the code at the boundary, bundles then looked up for links. Wired into product delete (detail + list) and variant delete.

## Three things I had to fix to make it work

1. `min={1}` on the quantity input made the browser block the submit event before validation ran, so AC3 showed a native tooltip instead of our message. Attributes removed; schema is the only place the rules live.
2. `FetchError` in the JS SDK threw away the `type` and `code` the server sends and kept only `message`, so **no** dashboard code could branch on an error code. AC7 needs it; fixed with two tests.
3. `vite.config.mts` never defined `__MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE__`. `file-upload.tsx` reads it as a bare global at module load, so the standalone dev server threw before React mounted — blank page, feature not demoable at all. I added the define. Proof rather than assertion: the identifier survives into the built bundle 5 times without it, 0 times with it. This is outside AC1–7 and I've flagged it under Tech Debt (Encountered) so you can drop it if you'd rather keep the diff clean.

Real bug — only a live call surfaces it. A bare `metadata` switches the API to "only these fields", so the edit form would open blank. Fixing with a guard test:

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-11-19 03:53:43Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Fix the fields constant and add guard tests

```bash
cd /Users/alexgrapsas/medusa-114 && python3 - <<'PY'
import io
p="packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/products/common/bundles.ts"
s=io.open(p,encoding="utf-8").read()
old='''/**
 * The fields the bundle edit form needs. It is what the full product edit flow
 * asks for, plus the metadata that holds the component list.
 */
export const BUNDLE_EDIT_FIELDS = `${PRODUCT_EDIT_FULL_FIELDS},metadata`'''
new='''/**
 * The fields the bundle edit form needs: what the full product edit flow asks
 * for, plus the metadata that holds the component list.
 *
 * The `+` matters. A bare field name switches the API from "the default fields
 * plus these relations" to "only these fields", which drops `title`, `handle`
 * and the rest of the product's own columns and opens the form empty. `+`
 * adds to the defaults instead.
 */
export const BUNDLE_EDIT_FIELDS = `${PRODUCT_EDIT_FULL_FIELDS},+metadata`'''
assert old in s
io.open(p,"w",encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(old,new,1))

p2="packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/products/common/__tests__/bundles.spec.ts"
s2=io.open(p2,encoding="utf-8").read()
s2=s2.replace('''import {
  BUNDLE_IN_USE_ERROR_CODE,''','''import {
  BUNDLE_EDIT_FIELDS,
  BUNDLE_IN_USE_ERROR_CODE,''',1)
s2 += '''
describe("BUNDLE_EDIT_FIELDS", () => {
  /*
   * A bare field name in `fields` makes the API return only the fields listed,
   * so `title`, `handle` and the product's other columns disappear and the edit
   * form opens empty. Every entry has to be prefixed with `*` (a relation) or
   * `+` (added to the defaults). Checked against the running API with
   * `GET /admin/products/:id?fields=...`: with `,metadata` the response had 10
   * keys and no title, with `,+metadata` it had 32 and kept everything.
   */
  it("asks for metadata without dropping the product's own fields", () => {
    expect(BUNDLE_EDIT_FIELDS.split(",")).toContain("+metadata")
    expect(BUNDLE_EDIT_FIELDS.split(",")).not.toContain("metadata")
  })

  it("prefixes every field it asks for", () => {
    const bare = BUNDLE_EDIT_FIELDS.split(",").filter(
      (field) => !field.startsWith("*") && !field.startsWith("+")
    )

    expect(bare).toEqual([])
  })
})
'''
io.open(p2,"w",encoding="utf-8").write(s2)
print("ok")

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-11-19 03:55:11Z)**_

The live run is done, and it found one bug my unit tests couldn't.

## End-to-end against a real backend

Booted the server on :9001 against a fresh `medusa_bundle_demo` DB and sent the exact bodies the two forms build:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `POST /admin/bundles` (create form's body) | 200, bundle created — **AC1** |
| `GET /admin/products/:id` (what the product page section reads) | `metadata.bundle.components` = `[{camera, 1}, {lens, 2}]`, 1 variant, `usd 89900` — **AC5** |
| `DELETE /admin/products/:lens` | 400, `code: "bundle_in_use"`, `type: "not_allowed"`, message naming `"Camera kit"` + id — **AC7** |
| `POST /admin/bundles/:id` (edit form's body) | 200, lens quantity 2 → 3, read back from metadata — **AC2** |
| component that is itself a bundle | `Variant … can't be a bundle component because it belongs to a bundle.` — the exact string my AC4 test asserts — **AC4** |

The delete row matters most: it proves the whole chain I built — core-flows tags the error, the HTTP handler passes `code` through, the js-sdk `FetchError` now keeps it, the dashboard matches on it.

## The bug it found

`BUNDLE_EDIT_FIELDS` asked for `,metadata`. A **bare** field name makes the API return *only* the fields listed instead of defaults-plus-relations — the response came back with 10 keys and no `title` or `handle`. **The edit form would have opened empty.**

Every unit test passed because they hand the product object straight to `mapBundleToFormValues` and never go through the API. It's `,+metadata` now (32 keys, verified), plus two tests pinning the rule that every field in that constant carries a `*` or `+` prefix.

That's the fourth thing a run caught that reading didn't — after the `min={1}` native-validation issue, the `FetchError` gap, and `zodResolver`.

## Final state

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `@medusajs/dashboard` (Vitest) | 47 files, **306 passed** |
| `@medusajs/core-flows` (Jest) | 11 suites, **223 passed** |
| `@medusajs/medusa` (Jest) | 16 suites, **146 passed** |
| `@medusajs/js-sdk` (Jest) | 4 suites, **33 passed** |
| `@medusajs/utils` (Jest) | 100 suites, **528 passed**, 1 skipped |
| `yarn build` | 81 of 81 |
| Dashboard typecheck / ESLint / `vite build` | clean |
| Prettier | same 4 pre-existing warnings as the base, none in lines I changed |

55 files, +4847/−100, uncommitted on `feat/issue-114-bundle-admin-screens` in `~/medusa-114`.

AC3 and AC6 aren't in the live table, and I'd rather say so than imply coverage I don't have: AC3 is browser behaviour with no request to make (covered by 31 component tests through the real schema and resolver), and AC6 needs an order with a part-returned bundle line, which is #117's territory — it's tested against the return-item shape #113 saves.

PR description is at `~/csci535-notes/pr-114-description.md`, updated with the live table and the fields bug.

Two things left running that you may want: the server on :9001 (admin `admin@test.com` / `supersecret`) with a "Camera kit v2" bundle already in it, and the demo script at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-alexgrapsas-medusa/deadae0e-1582-4505-885c-d35f48a4d684/scratchpad/demo.sh`. Pair it with `VITE_MEDUSA_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:9001 yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard dev --port 5174` and the screens should load without the stash — that's what the vite fix buys. `medusa-postgres` and `~/my-store` are still offline; `medusa-pg`/`medusa-redis` were already up before I started.

The dashboard reads `metadata.bundle_component.variant_id` and the return item's `quantity`; #117's own merged tests in `bundle-refunds.spec.ts` assert that `prepareBundleReturnItems` writes exactly that, in a dozen places. So the field names cannot drift silently in either direction, and what is untested is the wiring between them, not the shape. Building an order with a part-returned bundle line to close that last step is deliberately left for the return form work (criteria 8 to 10), which needs the same fixture."""
assert old2 in s
s = s.replace(old2, new2, 1)
io.open(p,"w",encoding="utf-8").write(s)
print("ok")
PY
```
